paper_title: Sensor-Based Detection of Organic Micropollutants Relevant to Urban Runoff: A Critical Review
paper_abstract: Urban runoff transports chemically diverse organic micropollutants from traffic surfaces, construction materials, consumer products, industrial areas, and atmospheric deposition into receiving waters. This review evaluates sensor-based approaches for selected pollutant classes relevant to urban runoff, with emphasis on per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), organophosphate esters (OPEs), tire-derived contaminants (TDCs), brominated flame retardants (BFRs), and benzothiazoles (BTs). Optical, electrochemical, photoelectrochemical, mass-sensitive, and biorecognition-based platforms are compared with respect to recognition chemistry, analytical range, limit of detection, and reported validation context. Molecularly imprinted polymers, nanostructured interfaces, aptamers, proteins, antibodies, and supramolecular receptors enable high analytical sensitivity, but practical performance in stormwater is determined by matrix tolerance, selectivity, recovery, fouling, calibration stability, fabrication reproducibility, and agreement with reference methods. The 75 representative sensor entries compiled for comparison comprise 39 PFAS, 15 BFR, 8 TDC, 7 OPE, and 6 BT entries; these counts describe the evidence set rather than publication frequencies. Information demonstrating systematic validation in authentic urban runoff, paired LC-MS/MS or GC-MS comparison, long-term stability, and multianalyte operation was limited or incompletely reported for many platforms. A complementary bibliometric analysis of 813 unique Web of Science Core Collection records (2016-July 2026) yielded a 386-term network in 12 clusters and indicated later average publication years for PFAS, 6PPD, and several advanced-sensing-related terms. The combined evidence indicates that the principal barrier to application is no longer analytical sensitivity alone, but reliable transfer of laboratory sensor performance to chemically and physically variable stormwater matrices through robust validation, standardized reporting, and field-compatible sample handling.

paper_title: Agentic AI in Payments and Financial Transactions: A Survey of Architectures, Safeguards and Open Problems
paper_abstract: AI agents powered by large language models are beginning to initiate, authorize, and execute financial transactions on behalf of users and institutions. Between 2024 and 2026 the industry shipped the first payment infrastructure purpose-built for this shift: Google's Agent Payments Protocol (AP2), Coinbase's x402, Visa Intelligent Commerce, and Mastercard Agent Pay, while central banks began experimenting with agentic systems inside wholesale payment infrastructures. Yet the academic literature has not synthesized this transition: existing surveys cover LLM agents generally and financial applications of LLMs broadly, but none examine the specific problem of agents that move money. This survey provides a structured review of agentic AI in payments and financial transactions. We analyze 54 primary works spanning agent architectures, production payment protocols, central-bank research, agent identity frameworks, adversarial security literature, and liability scholarship. We propose a four-axis taxonomy (autonomy level, transaction authority, guarantee mechanism, and failure surface) and use it to map every surveyed system. We find that transaction-integrity guarantees such as idempotency, settlement finality, and reconciliation are enforced largely by convention rather than by structure; that machine-verifiable mandates and agent identity remain immature; and that liability allocation for agent-initiated transactions is unresolved across jurisdictions. We conclude with a research agenda covering bounded-autonomy mechanisms, payment-aware agent benchmarks, machine-verifiable mandates, and systemic-risk modelling. A living bibliography accompanies this survey.

paper_title: A Narrative Review of Fetal Tumors- I: Diagnosis and Management of Head, Neck, Orbital and Oral Tumors
paper_abstract: Fetal tumors (benign and malignant) are uncommon, diverse and vary in presentation, time of diagnosis and outcome. Tumors of the head, neck, mouth and eyes are some of the more common and include teratomas, craniopharyngiomas, lipomas, retinoblastomas and tumors of the choroid plexus. Some of these tumors are difficult to diagnose prenatally and indeed are only diagnosed after delivery although they appear first in-utero. With advances in imaging, identifying these tumors prenatally is improving. Because these tumors are uncommon, it would not be unusual for clinicians not to have come across some of them. In this review we present some of the more common fetal tumors including their ultrasound features (with clues on how to make a diagnosis), associated genetic or structural abnormalities, how to monitor and manage affected fetuses, prognosis and recurrence risk which should inform counselling of parents. For most of these tumors, consideration must be given to accurately defining the extent of the lesions with MRI to allow for planned treatment which is commonly in the form of surgical excision. A number of these tumors will require combination therapy of surgical excision and chemotherapy or radiotherapy. The prognosis for most of them is good depending largely in most cases on the involvement of adjacent structures and the effect of the tumors on adjacent structures.

paper_title: Body-Centered Interaction in VR Narrative Storytelling: A Systematic Literature Review
paper_abstract: Virtual reality narratives increasingly use bodily participation to shape how stories unfold and are experienced. This systematic review examines the narrative functions of bodily mechanisms and the theories and evidence used to explain them in VR and related spatially embodied AR/MR environments. Searches of Web of Science, Scopus, IEEE Xplore, and ACM Digital Library identified 370 reports published between January 2015 and April 2026. Cinematic VR and 360-degree embodiment, avatar embodiment and perspective-taking, and locomotion were the primary foci in 219 of 367 RQ1 reports. Substantive theoretical use appeared in 340 reports, including 44 with explicit cross-family integration. Comparative or associational evidence appeared in 232 reports; 54 contributed methodological diagnoses only. Close comparison of 32 purposively selected reports examined how bodily configurations acquire narrative functions and how designed cues relate to participant interpretations. Body-Centered Narrative Coherence (BCNC) brings these relations into an analytical framework organized through bodily anchoring, theoretical congruence, and empirical traceability.

paper_title: A Comparative Study of Unmanned Surface Vessel and Manned-Vessel Single-Beam Echosounder Surveys for Bathymetry in a Coastal Environment
paper_abstract: Unmanned surface vessels (USVs) are increasingly used for nearshore bathymetry, yet their interchangeability with manned-vessel surveys is rarely tested on identical lines. We compared single-beam echosounder surveys from a 1.4 m USV and a 3 m manned vessel over 13,287 m² of a shallow estuarine canal entrance in Queensland, Australia, using the same 8 m transects and real-time kinematic positioning on consecutive days. Agreement at 191 co-located samples was assessed using robust statistics, transect-clustered bootstrap confidence intervals (CIs), spatial autocorrelation and the International Hydrographic Organization (IHO) S-44 Order 1a total vertical uncertainty. Neither the bias (0.06 m; 95% CI −0.03 to 0.14 m) nor the net volume difference (30 ± 2600 m³) differed significantly from zero, but the 95% limits of agreement spanned −0.66 to 0.78 m. Differences were largest at the shallow survey margin (mean 0.39 m) and were spatially correlated over about 50 m, more than halving the effective sample size. Compliance with the combined Order 1a allowance (93–100% by depth range) could not be distinguished statistically from the 95% criterion. The USV surveyed three times faster, but the resulting level of detection of about 0.7 m means mixed-platform monitoring requires overlap surveys, crosslines and positioning quality control.

paper_title: Machine Learning and Deep Learning for Depression Detection from Behavioral Signals: A Survey of Modalities, Datasets, and Evaluation Practices
paper_abstract: Machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) methods for detecting depression, classifying diagnostic status, and estimating symptom severity from behavioral signals have expanded rapidly, yet the resulting evidence base is difficult to compare because studies differ in input modality, dataset provenance, label definition, task formulation, evaluation design, and metric reporting. This survey systematically maps the field along these computational dimensions. Following a PRISMA 2020-aligned workflow, we searched Web of Science, Scopus, and IEEE Xplore (21 November 2025), screened 7,369 records, and included 195 studies that train and evaluate ML/DL models on audio/speech, text/language, and/or video/vision inputs, yielding 329 study-by-dataset entries and 1,039 extracted metric entries. We organize the literature with a six-dimensional taxonomy covering input modality, representation strategy, architecture family, fusion strategy, task and label formulation, and evaluation protocol, and we quantify the prevalence of each category under a strict explicit-only extraction protocol. The corpus is recent (71.3% of studies from 2022–2025), predominantly single-modality (72.0% of entries), and text-centered (41.6%); pretrained representations dominate (42.2%), and transformers, convolutional networks, and recurrent networks form the leading architecture tier. Binary depression-status classification outweighs continuous severity estimation, labels are grounded mainly in PHQ- and BDI-based instruments rather than formal diagnoses, and the DAIC/AVEC family accounts for 24.9% of dataset entries. After harmonizing class-specific and variant metric names, reporting concentrates on F1, accuracy, precision, and recall. However, 71.4% of entries lack explicit model–metric–context binding and 76.9% lack a clearly extractable primary metric. We conclude that the literature supports structural synthesis but not leaderboard-style claims of model superiority, and we distill open challenges and a minimum reporting checklist for future primary studies.

paper_title: When Peer Review Does Not Reach Closure: Generative AI, Critique Inflation, and the Editorial Stopping Problem
paper_abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) makes candidate criticism inexpensive to produce, while verification, revision, and editorial attention remain costly. A manuscript may consequently improve across revision rounds even as the volume of critique fails to decrease. We define critique inflation as growth or persistence in candidate or optional critique without a corresponding increase in material deficiencies. A theoretical framework distinguishes verified material concerns, verified non-blocking improvements, and invalid or unsubstantiated candidates. Raw comment counts can depend on the critique prompt as well as on manuscript deficiencies. An editorial selectivity condition shows that, under a positive lower bound on per-comment response burden, bounded non-material author burden requires the fraction of optional comments converted into mandatory requests to scale at most inversely with their supply. The revision model \( D_{k+1}=\rho D_k+u_k \) yields a threshold \( u^\star=(1-\rho)\varepsilon \) for newly added mandatory load. A uniform bound below this threshold guarantees finite-time entry into the acceptance region of the model; persistent load at or above it can prevent entry. Verified decisive objections retain their scientific force independently of their provenance. The framework provides operational indicators and motivates testable hypotheses for multi-round, AI-assisted peer review.

paper_title: Selenium and Autoimmune Thyroid Disease: Mechanistic Insights and Clinical Evidence—A Scoping Review
paper_abstract: Autoimmune thyroid disease (AITD), comprising Hashimoto’s thyroiditis (HT) and Graves–Basedow disease (GBD), is the leading cause of acquired thyroid dysfunction, and selenium is essential for selenoprotein-mediated antioxidant defense in the thyroid. This scoping review, reported according to PRISMA-ScR, mapped the human evidence on selenium and, secondarily, myo-inositol across the AITD spectrum in adults. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, Google Scholar, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched (January 1996–October 2026), and methodological quality was appraised with standardized tools. Of 139 records identified (75 after deduplication), 43 sources were charted: 20 primary studies, 17 systematic reviews/meta-analyses, and 6 narrative reviews. Selenium consistently lowered thyroid peroxidase antibody titers in HT (pooled standardized mean differences, −0.80 to −4.94). However, the two largest randomized controlled trials, in HT (n = 412) and GBD (n = 430), showed no benefit on quality of life, remission, or thyroid function. A reproducible clinical benefit was confirmed only in mild Graves’ orbitopathy. Myo-inositol plus selenium lowered thyrotropin more than selenium alone in subclinical hypothyroidism, although this evidence is limited. Thus, selenium lowers thyroid autoantibodies without patient-relevant benefit in AITD, except in mild Graves’ orbitopathy; trials in early-stage disease with validated quality-of-life outcomes are needed.

paper_title: Effect of Intravitreal Injections on Intraocular Pressure: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
paper_abstract: Background: Intravitreal injection (IVT) is increasing in daily practice of ophthalmologists. Different medications were used in this injection which had side effects. One of these side effects is increase in intraocular pressure (IOP). Objective: The primary objective of this systematic review is to assess the prevalence and percentage of increase/change of IOP after IVT. Secondary objectives include identifying risk factors for IOP change after IVT, practical guidelines for the management of increased IOP, and comparing the effects of different medications on IOP. Methods: A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted according to PRISMA and MOOSE guidelines. PubMed, Embase, Google Scholar, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched for studies published between January 2020 and October 2025. Random-effects meta-analysis was performed to estimate mean differences (MDs) in IOP following intravitreal injection. Results: A total of 26 studies were included. Baseline pooled IOP was 16.26 ± 6.07 mmHg. Compared with baseline, IOP increased significantly immediately after intravitreal in-jection (MD 19.68 mmHg, 95% CI 15.36–23.99; P < 0.0001), remained elevated at 30 minutes (MD 4.47 mmHg, 95% CI 2.81–6.12; P < 0.0001), and was still significantly higher at 1 hour (MD 5.09 mmHg, 95% CI 0.25–9.94; P = 0.0419). Similar findings were observed for anti-VEGF injections, with aflibercept demonstrating the largest immediate increase in IOP. Conclusion: Intravitreal injections are associated with a significant but transient elevation in IOP, with the greatest increase occurring immediately after injection. Although IOP decreases over time, elevated levels may persist for up to one hour. Careful post-injection monitoring is recommended, particularly in patients at increased risk of glaucoma or ocular hypertension.

paper_title: Closed-Form Evaluations of Partial and Complete Bell Polynomials: A Classified Survey
paper_abstract: The partial Bell polynomials \(B_{n,k}\), also known as the Bell polynomials of the second kind, and the complete Bell polynomials Yn are the coefficients in the Faà di Bruno formula and in the exponential of a power series. Many problems in combinatorics, number theory, and analysis reduce to evaluating them at specific sequences. This survey collects the results on these polynomials in Comtet’s book Advanced Combinatorics, correcting two misprints there, together with the closed-form evaluations obtained in the papers and preprints of the second author and his coauthors and in related literature. The evaluations are classified, following the scheme of Qi, Niu, Lim, and Yao [J. Math. Anal. Appl. 491 (2020), Art. 124382] by the sequence or function at which the polynomials are evaluated: exponential, logarithmic, and power functions, square roots, trigonometric and hyperbolic functions and their inverses, sinc functions, products of sine and hyperbolic sine, factorials, natural numbers, Stirling, Lah, harmonic, Catalan, Fibonacci, Bernoulli, and Euler numbers, and several more. We also survey a general principle that turns series expansions of integer powers of a function, or of its normalized remainders, into such evaluations, together with recent work on normalized remainders. As a new result, we evaluate the partial Bell polynomials at the reciprocals \(1/\binom{q+i}{i}\) of binomial coefficients in terms of the \(q\)-associated Stirling numbers of the second kind; this gives the Maclaurin coefficients of every real power of the normalized remainders \(T_{q-1}[e^x]\) and unifies explicit formulas for the Bernoulli numbers, the generalized Bernoulli numbers, and Howard's numbers. We also prove, by differential Galois theory, that the Gauss hypergeometric function \({}_{2}F_1\bigl(\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2};2;t\bigr)\) behind Oertel's problem is not elementary, which answers a question posed in 2022. We also survey applications to special numbers and polynomials, ordinary differential equations, Gauss hypergeometric functions, multiple zeta values, and Hoffman's and Genˇcev's combinatorial identities. Proofs are omitted, except for those of the new results, and several open problems are posed and partially solved: we reduce Oertel's problem along each diagonal to a polynomial of fixed degree, give determinantal expressions for its coefficients, and prove by singularity analysis that along each column they are not hypergeometric terms, characterize the functions at whose derivatives the values of \(B_{n,k}\) satisfy linear recurrences with polynomial coefficients as the D-finite functions, express the partial Bell polynomials at \((0,\dotsc,0,s,s+1,\dotsc)\) as \((s-2)\)-fold sums of the Stirling numbers \(S(n,k)\), prove for \(s \ge 4\) that no single sum \(\sum_{j\ge0}w(n,k,j)S(n-aj,k-bj)\) with hypergeometric weights exists when \(b \ge 1\), nor for broad classes of weights when \(b \le 0\), and state the remaining case as a conjecture, evaluate \(\sum_{j=k}^{n}s(n,j)\alpha^jS(j,k)\) for \(\alpha=3\), \(\alpha=\frac{1}{3}\), and \(\alpha=-3\) by single sums, and determine all \(\alpha\) for which these sums are hypergeometric terms in \(n\).

paper_title: Predictors of AI Chatbot Use for Mental Health Support: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
paper_abstract: OBJECTIVE To systematically review and quantitatively synthesize the evidence on the predictors of the use of artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots for mental health support. METHOD We searched PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science, in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines, for quantitative studies that examined factors associated with the use of AI chatbots for mental health support. We assessed the methodological quality of the studies with the revised Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal tool for analytical cross-sectional studies. We pooled adjusted odds ratios (ORs) with random-effects models for predictors that had been examined in at least three studies, and we performed several sensitivity analyses. RESULTS We included eight cross-sectional studies with 7864 participants from the United States, Greece and Canada. Mental health service use (pooled OR = 1.62, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.33 to 1.98), depressive symptoms (pooled OR = 1.65, 95% CI = 1.38 to 1.98) and Asian race (pooled OR = 1.87, 95% CI = 1.46 to 2.41) were associated with higher odds of AI chatbot use for mental health support, and these associations were robust in all sensitivity analyses. Anxiety symptoms, younger age and Hispanic ethnicity were also associated with higher odds of use, although these associations were not robust in sensitivity analyses. Sex, suicidality and Black race were not associated with use, while the frequency of use among users was not associated with sex or mental health service use. CONCLUSIONS Individuals who already use mental health services and those with depressive symptoms are more likely to use AI chatbots for mental health support, which suggests that these tools may be used alongside, rather than instead of, professional care.

paper_title: Gender-Based Violence and Artificial Intelligence: An Interdisciplinary Survey with a Focus on Iran and Persian NLP
paper_abstract: Gender-based violence is a major public health and human rights concern that affects millions of people worldwide. Understanding this type of violence requires examining not only the acts themselves, but also the social norms, cultural beliefs, and legal institutions that shape how violence is justified, reported, and addressed. Artificial intelligence offers new opportunities to study these issues through large collections of textual data. However, identifying violence-related language does not necessarily establish what occurred, who was responsible, or whether a speaker is reporting, justifying, or condemning violence. We combine psychological, sociological, legal, media, and natural language processing research, focusing on Iran and related contexts in Persian. We introduce a construct translation framework tracing how experiences of violence may be represented through disclosure, documentation, dataset selection, annotation, model outputs, and subsequent use. One objective is to identify where information about speakers, context, evidentiary status, and uncertainty may be lost or misinterpreted. This review clarifies the limitations of present AI methods and recommends culturally informed annotation, evaluations that assess whether models detect what they claim to detect, clear documentation of evidence sources, and more involvement of relevant experts and communities.

paper_title: Weight-Space Programming with Large Language Models: A Survey
paper_abstract: Weight-space programming (WSP) uses a large language model (LLM), often as a coding agent, to read, write or edit another neural network's weights directly, without training it. After a November 2026 MIT CSAIL blog post showed a frontier LLM raising a small model's math score from 8% to 48% by editing its weights, 70 reports followed within three weeks, whose different setups and controls make claims hard to compare. This survey reviews these first 70 reports, including 54 primary studies, and links every extracted claim to a verbatim passage in its source. It distinguishes WSP from fine-tuning, model editing, activation steering, weight-space learning and LLM-as-optimizer methods; proposes a four-axis taxonomy (operation, protocol, mechanism and scope); maps 11 application areas; and audits the controls, baselines and failure modes behind the claims. Three findings emerge. First, LLMs can write small networks from scratch when the task has a short program. Second, apparent reading of weights often rests on surface cues. Third, many reported repairs are simple: a simpler method matched the LLM on at least one task in 34 of 54 primary studies, WSP beat its strongest simple comparator in only 4, and only 13 tested a fix that changes no weights. In a controlled case study of the original MIT repair, the edit gives a real gain, but switching off thinking mode, which changes no weights, recovers 94% of it with 36% of the edited model's tokens; fine-tuning on a larger model's solutions recovers 86%. The survey closes with WSP-12, a twelve-item reporting checklist, and open problems; the coded corpus is public.

paper_title: Applications of Capillary Electrophoresis in the Simultaneous Determination of Oral Antidiabetic Drugs in Pharmaceutical Formulations and Biological Samples: A Review
paper_abstract: The increasing use of fixed-dose combinations in the treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus presents analytical challenges due to differences in the physicochemical properties and concentration ratios of the active pharmaceutical ingredients. Capillary electrophoresis (CE) offers an alternative to chromatographic methods, with advantages including high separation efficiency and low reagent and analyte consumption. This review examines the application of CE to the simultaneous determination of oral antidiabetic drugs in pharmaceutical formulations and biological samples, focusing on separation conditions, analytical performance, and method limitations. A structured literature search covering publications from January 2001 to November 2026 was conducted using PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect. Studies describing CE-based methods for the simultaneous analysis of oral antidiabetic drugs, including combinations with other pharmaceutical compounds, were considered. The reviewed methods included capillary zone electrophoresis (CZE), micellar electrokinetic chromatography (MEKC), non-aqueous capillary electrophoresis (NACE), microemulsion electrokinetic chromatography (MEEKC), and CE coupled with mass spectrometry (CE-MS). CZE was mainly applied to pharmaceutical formulations, including combinations with drug dosage ratios of up to 500:1, while MEKC provided additional selectivity for mixtures containing neutral analytes. Fewer studies addressed biological samples, where CE-MS and on-line preconcentration techniques were used to improve detection sensitivity. Overall, CE has demonstrated its applicability to the simultaneous determination of oral antidiabetic drugs, particularly in pharmaceutical formulations. However, applications to clinical samples remain limited, and further studies are needed to establish the suitability of these methods for routine analysis.

paper_title: Epidemiological Contagion Models Supported by Machine Learning: A Critical Review of Hybrid Mechanistic–Data-Driven Approaches
paper_abstract: Although the parameters are interpretable, mechanistic compartmental models (SIR, SEIR, SIS) are not realistic for complex, rapidly changing epidemics because they assume homogeneous mixing and constant parameters. Machine learning (ML) can learn nonlinear dynamics and can assimilate heterogeneous mobility, environmental, clinical and socioeconomic data. This narrative overview focuses on the use of ML to develop compartment, stochastic, network-based and agent-based models, as well as spatiotemporal forecasting, mobility-driven transmission, risk mapping of epidemics, planning for healthcare resources, and simulation of policies, with a particular focus on hybrid mechanistic–data-driven models that maintain the interpretability of epidemiology. The difficulties of purely data-driven approaches are illustrated using a supplemental case study of the performance of persistence, linear autoregression, and random forests for 7-day-smoothed daily COVID-19 cases in the United States over a 228-day test period. All models achieve an R² ≈ 0.98 for a 1-day forecast horizon when hyperparameter tuning is done independently for each horizon. At each horizon, however, none did as well as the persistence baseline. The best-tuned random forest had an MAE of 2,384 at 1 day, while persistence had an MAE of 2,144 (11% worse); at 14 days, the random forest was 35% worse. All six comparisons supported persistence in favor of Diebold–Mariano intervals and block-bootstrap intervals. This illustrative example shows that informative covariates, hybrid structures and careful evaluation are necessary in order to outperform simple baselines for generic learners. Other subjects covered are uncertainty quantification, interpretability, data bias, privacy, and governance. We think the best route to real-time public health decision support is hybrid systems that report uncertainty, are open, and are subject to simple baselines.

paper_title: Visibility Bias in AI-Based Underwater Fish Monitoring: A Scoping Review of Ecological Validity and a Reporting Checklist
paper_abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly detects and counts fish in underwater imagery, but turbidity, light attenuation, low light, and distance affect which fish are visible. Ecology treats this as imperfect detection; the AI literature mostly treats it as an image-quality problem. This PRISMA-ScR scoping review coded 183 AI studies (2015–2026), identified through structured and database searches and evaluated on field-monitoring imagery from natural waters, on five dimensions of the observation process: visibility characterization, data independence, external-domain robustness, calibration and false-positive control, and ecological endpoint validation. A language model coded each study twice; the first author checked 90 studies (49%) against the full text, and the second author's blind coding of 40 randomly sampled studies agreed with 87% of its ratings. No study reported performance stratified by measured visibility, and only two measured water clarity with an instrument. Training and test data were separated by video, day, site, or region in 58 studies (32%); 18 (10%) compared the same model inside and outside its training domain; none reported a standard calibration metric; and 59 (32%) linked outputs to an ecological quantity, only 6 against a reference independent of the imagery. We propose a draft eleven-item reporting checklist (MRCUAI) and research agenda.

paper_title: A Survey of Security, Privacy, and Ethics of Large Language Models in Telecom
paper_abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into telecommunications for customer service, network analytics, and operational support. While offering efficiency and innovation, their deployment raises critical privacy, security, and ethical challenges due to the uniquely sensitive and longitudinal nature of telecom data. This paper presents a survey of LLM risks and safeguards in telecom context. Our survey introduces a telecom-specific taxonomy linking privacy, security, and ethics with use cases and outlines open research challenges such as longitudinal data privacy, cross-border compliance, and scalable guardrails.
comments: 5 pages, 1 figure, published in COMSNETS 2025 conference

paper_title: How Much Effort Does an AI Code Reviewer Need? Evidence from Claude 5.5 Models on Plausible-but-Wrong Patches
paper_abstract: AI coding agents write code faster than people can review it, so teams add AI reviewers. Reasoning models let such a reviewer trade cost for diligence through an effort setting. We asked how much effort a reviewer needs to catch plausible-but-wrong patches, which pass a benchmark's tests but fail stronger ones. Claude Opus 5.5 (preregistered), Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 (exploratory) each reviewed the same 90 agent-written Django patches from SWE-bench Verified at low, medium and high effort. By strengthened SWE-ABS tests, 55 patches were wrong and 35 correct. In every model, high effort accepted fewer wrong patches than low (false success .45 against .67 for Opus, .49 against .65 for Sonnet, .51 against .78 for Haiku), a supported difference for Opus and Haiku. For Opus, medium was non-inferior to high within 15 percentage points (difference .018, 95% CI [-.065, .108]) and cost 20% less, short of the preregistered 30%. For Sonnet and Haiku, medium cost 39% and 51% less than high but was not shown non-inferior. Opus at medium or high agreed best with the labels; Haiku at high cost about 8% as much per review as Opus at medium, accuracy difference unresolved. Exploratory coding showed that most rejections named the tested defect and that effort added such rejections. No setting is a strong gate: each accepted at least 45% of wrong patches. For 32 of the 55 wrong patches the issue may not require what the failing test checks; without them, neither accuracy hypothesis holds for any model.
comments: 18 pages, 7 figures. Preregistered at https://osf.io/r8q2m. Data and code: https://github.com/trustmybot/research-artifacts

paper_title: PeerReveal: Learning to Generalize in AI Peer Review Detection
paper_abstract: Can we distinguish fully AI-generated reviews from those using AI only to rewrite human judgement? Furthermore, can we do so reliably when reviews are generated from diverse AI models and workflows across scientific domains? To this end, we introduce PeerReveal, a new detector that grounds its decisions in learned relationships between a review's claims and reference claims drawn from AI-generated reviews of the same paper, complemented by review-level textual signals. We evaluate PeerReveal on PeerShift, a new, challenging test set of 5,430 reviews spanning multiple domains, including machine learning, life sciences, and social sciences, combining variation in disciplinary review conventions with diverse AI review-production mechanisms. With regular training, PeerReveal achieves 70.52% pooled Macro-F1 on this benchmark, improving over the strongest baseline by 11.48 points. We develop an effective and practical adversarial training framework that further improves the detector's generalization using a small local generator optimized to produce challenging reviews, raising pooled Macro-F1 from 70.52% to 82.40%. These results show that robust AI-review detection benefits from richer review-level evidence and adversarial training on more challenging generation processes.

paper_title: Toward Decision-Native Language Models: A Review of Architectures, Reliability and Challenges
paper_abstract: Software systems increasingly invoke language models on closed questions, such as assigning a support ticket to a team, screening whether a tool call is safe, or selecting a model to answer a query. Unlike open-ended chat, these calls require a fast, inexpensive and trustworthy probability distribution over a declared answer set. Following the 2026 release of Jev and subsequent open typed decision models, empirical findings remain scattered across separate literatures on prompt calibration, option-order bias, uncertainty estimation, routing, guardrails and automated judging. Here we trace the architectural progression from prompted generation and token-logit readouts to decision-native designs, evaluate whether their output probabilities are calibrated, invariant and robust, and examine how these components behave inside routers, guardrails, judges and agents. Using five falsifiable criteria for decision-native architectures and six comparison axes, we show that open models read out at label tokens already recover most of the accuracy credited to dedicated decision models. Decision-native designs primarily deliver substantial latency and cost reductions alongside structural order invariance in option-isolated variants, whereas calibration, probabilistic coherence and adversarial robustness vary sharply across domains. We conclude with an evaluation critique, a role-by-role readiness rubric and priorities for null-aware, coherent and traceable decision models.

paper_title: Selected Topics in Differential Geometry in Biophysics and Medical Physics: A Review of Five Domains
paper_abstract: Biological morphology, molecular mechanics, medical image analysis, and physiological wave propagation frequently obey constraints that are intrinsically geometric rather than Euclidean. This article develops a unified geometric perspective across five selected domains of continuum biophysics and clinical medical physics. First, we explore extrinsic surface geometry, Canham–Helfrich and area-difference elasticity, and Gauss–Bonnet topological barriers in lipid membranes and viral scission. Second, we examine principal \(\mathrm{SO}(3)\) Cosserat frame bundles, twist connections, and the Călugăreanu–White–Fuller theorem in DNA supercoiling and isoform-specific topoisomerase pharmacology. Third, we cover the Cartan–Hadamard symmetric space \(\mathrm{Sym}^+(3) \cong \mathrm{GL}(3,\mathbb{R})/\mathrm{O}(3)\), Log-Euclidean similarity geometry, and multi-fiber spherical extensions in Diffusion MRI and neurosurgical tractography. Fourth, we discuss infinite-dimensional Sobolev metrics on diffeomorphism groups \(\mathrm{Diff}_V(\Omega)\), Euler–Poincaré (EPDiff) geodesic flows, and differential-form dose accumulation in computational anatomy and four-dimensional adaptive radiotherapy. Finally, we address principal gauge connections, Pancharatnam–Berry geometric phases, and topological phase defects in low-Reynolds-number motility, adiabatic MRI pulse design, and cardiac arrhythmia mapping. Alongside pedagogical derivations (collected in technical appendices), we critically compare competing physical models, evaluate numerical discretization pitfalls, uncertainty quantification, and phantom/clinical validation benchmarks, and clarify where idealized geometric invariants must be tempered by physiological dynamics and clinical trial evidence.

paper_title: An Update on the Biochemical Staging of Nutritional Rickets: A Comprehensive Review
paper_abstract: Nutritional rickets remains a significant global public health concern affecting infants and young children in regions with limited sunlight exposure or inadequate dietary vitamin D and calcium. This review revisits the biochemical staging system applicable to severe combined vitamin D and calcium deficiency. We propose that the classical three-stage model may be supplemented by recognition of a Nutritional Pseudohypoparathyroidism / PTH Resistance Variant—characterized by profound hypocalcemia, paradoxically normal or elevated serum phosphate, and markedly elevated parathyroid hormone (PTH)—reflecting acquired renal PTH resistance. Hypomagnesemia must be excluded before this designation is applied, as it constitutes a reversible and mechanistically distinct cause of functional PTH resistance. This phenotype is reversible with treatment and requires prospective validation. Evidence-based treatment strategies for each stage are summarized.

paper_title: Harvesting Solid Carbon from Catalytic Methane Pyrolysis: Removal Routes, Catalyst Make-Up and Carbon Value: A Data-Driven Review
paper_abstract: Catalytic methane pyrolysis forms no CO₂ directly and, by stoichiometry, makes 2.98 kg of solid carbon per kg of hydrogen; viability depends on removing the carbon, retaining the catalyst, selling the carbon and keeping it solid, because oxidizing all of it later would release 10.9 kg of CO₂ per kg of hydrogen, comparable to steam reforming. One acid wash of a 5 g sample retained 91–95% of the carbon with metal below the 50 ppm detection limit; carbon from bismuth-based melts carries 52–83 wt% metal unless salt-capped; gasification can restore catalyst activity, variably, but consumes the product. The longest reported operation exceeds 500 h cumulatively, in two moving-bed pilots. Published model estimates span $1.7–8.2 per kg of hydrogen without carbon sale and $0.8–4.1 with it (2023 USD); once-through catalyst make-up at the median laboratory carbon-to-catalyst ratio would add about $8.3. Reported emission intensities span 0–25 kg CO₂-eq per kg of hydrogen because boundaries, methane leakage, heat supply, and carbon credits differ; each 1% of upstream methane leakage adds at least 1.2 kg, and no assessment quantifies later oxidation of the carbon. We propose a design-for-harvest hypothesis map, a reporting checklist, data structures for machine learning, and emissions-accounting rules.

paper_title: A Scoping Review of Occupational Risk Assessment Methods: Classification, Advantages, Limitations and Application Areas
paper_abstract: Background: Occupational risk assessment is a mandatory procedure in modern occupational health and safety (OHS) management systems worldwide. However, no single regulatory document prescribes the use of a specific assessment method, leaving organizations with a wide choice of available tools. The diversity of existing approaches – from simple checklists to complex probabilistic models – creates a methodological challenge for practitioners and researchers, particularly in high-risk industries such as coal mining. Objectives: This scoping review aims to systematically map and classify existing occupational risk assessment methods, identify their key advantages and limitations and determine their typical application areas. The review also examines the regulatory requirements for risk assessment in Russian and international practice. Eligibility Criteria: The review included methods and approaches for occupational risk assessment published in peer-reviewed journals, regulatory documents and industry guidelines in English or Russian, supplemented by Persian-language sources indexed in Scopus and Web of Science, which were fully translated into English for de-tailed methodological review, over the past 30 years. Methods were included if they provided a structured approach to hazard identification, risk estimation or risk evaluation applicable to occupational settings. Sources of Evidence: A systematic search was conducted in Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar and Russian scientific databases (eLIBRARY.ru) using keywords related to occupational risk assessment, hazard identification and risk analysis methods. Charting Methods: Data were extracted using a standardized form and grouped by methodological principle into eleven thematic blocks. Each method was described in terms of its core principle, advantages, limitations and typical application areas. Results: Fifty-five distinct methods were identified and classified into eleven blocks: (1) qualitative hazard identification; (2) engineering reliability analysis; (3) scenario modeling and barrier analysis; (4) human reliability assessment; (5) semi-quantitative ranking methods; (6) probabilistic and statistical methods; (7) uncertainty and multi-criteria hybrids; (8) hygienic and health risk assessment; (9) ergonomic and biomechanical risks; (10) psychosocial risks; (11) behavioral safety and strategic management. A comparative analysis revealed that no single method is universally applicable; the choice depends on data availability, assessment objectives and organizational con-text. Conclusions: This scoping review provides a comprehensive map of existing occupational risk assessment methods, offering researchers and practitioners a structured framework for selecting appropriate tools based on their specific needs. The classification highlights the complementary nature of different approaches and the necessity of hybrid methodologies for complex industrial settings.

paper_title: Validating Generative Virtual Patients for Intended Medical AI Uses: A Critical Narrative Review
paper_abstract: Generative virtual patients (VPs) now support medical large language model training, interactive policy optimization, capability benchmarking, safety red-teaming, and clinical education. They are both evaluation objects and measurement instruments: source substrates, demographic distributions, and response policies shape training signals and evaluation conclusions. Their errors are not merely random noise; they may propagate as structured, configuration-dependent bias across the evidence-generation chain. Yet validation studies often assess script fidelity, fluency, inter-rater reliability, or case plausibility without testing how these measurements support downstream decisions. We synthesize evidence along a five-node chain: source substrate, patient information state and response policy, doctor–patient interaction, scoring and outcomes, and downstream decisions. Across this chain, local adequacy alone never licenses cross-setting extrapolation: disclosure policies determine which inquiry capabilities can be elicited, scoring reliability fails to guarantee construct validity, and case-level diagnostic coherence can coexist with population-level epidemiological distortion. Admission-time information loss and public-EHR case recall remain hypotheses requiring targeted audits, while simulated-user performance may fail to predict human interaction outcomes. Increasing the number of independent simulation runs reduces sampling variance but cannot resolve untested discrepancies from target clinical settings. We propose an intended-use validation framework that defines target estimands, tests decision-critical assumptions via paired temporal audits, clinically reviewed perturbations, and task-matched human references, and documents reuse boundaries in an Evaluation Provenance Statement. Before interactive evaluation standards solidify, validating specific simulator configurations for defined inferences—not VP technology in the abstract—is essential for credible medical AI training, benchmarking, governance, and algorithmovigilance.

paper_title: A Comprehensive Survey of Multi-Agent Systems Through a Layered Taxonomy Spanning Science, Engineering, and Applications
paper_abstract: Multi-agent systems have emerged as a dominant architectural paradigm for applied AI, yet deploying them effectively requires bridging scientific understanding of agent coordination with engineering constraints and real-world application demands. This survey presents a unified perspective on the multi-agent AI landscape, synthesizing research across the science of how multiple LLM-driven agents coordinate, the engineering of systems that implement that coordination under production constraints, and the application-level evidence of where such systems deliver measurable value. We introduce a layered taxonomy of multi-agent capabilities, spanning Agent Primitives, Coordination, Communication, Intelligence, and Assurance. We then organize 13 functionalities into 8 key concepts derived inductively from the literature, situated within the layered taxonomy of multi-agent capabilities: (Agent specialization, Orchestration patterns, Decision making, Context engineering, Learning, Evaluation, Tracing & Monitoring, and Security & Safety). For each concept, we trace its intellectual origins, survey current scientific findings, examine engineering design patterns, and ground the discussion in enterprise deployments. We motivate multi-agent architectures through an analysis of single-agent limitations (including context saturation, instruction-following degradation, tool selection noise, and limited modularity) while acknowledging that multi-agent decomposition is not universally superior and introduces its own coordination overhead. We identify principled criteria for when multi-agent coordination is justified over single-agent designs, and examine the responsible AI mechanisms necessary for trustworthy operation at scale. We conclude by outlining directions for future research on open challenges, including evaluation difficulty, cost efficiency, emergent security threats, and governance in a rapidly shifting regulatory landscape.

paper_title: Third-Space Optimisation (3SO) in Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Narrative Review and Proposed Framework for Integrating the Patellofemoral Joint into Alignment Planning
paper_abstract: Total knee arthroplasty (TKA) planning has centred on tibiofemoral alignment and balance, with the patellofemoral joint assessed only after tibiofemoral decisions have been made. Yet anterior knee pain remains a leading contributor to dissatisfaction after TKA. This narrative review synthesises the biomechanical, imaging and clinical literature on patellofemoral mechanics in TKA (PubMed, MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane Library; 1990–2026) and, on that basis, proposes Third-Space Optimisation (3SO): a patellofemoral constraint layer applied within any existing alignment strategy rather than a new alignment philosophy. The evidence shows that patellofemoral kinematics are sensitive to femoral axial rotation, mediolateral femoral position, tibial component orientation and implantation depth — variables that no current strategy targets collectively. Because tibiofemoral balance can be achieved through multiple component configurations, a solution space exists within which patellofemoral consequences can be weighed. We identify the anterior chamfer zone (approximately 20–60° of flexion) as an intraoperative blind spot and argue that the distal femoral morphotype, rather than global limb alignment, may drive patellofemoral risk. Patellar resurfacing cannot compensate for suboptimal component positioning. A descriptive stepwise pathway and a research agenda are presented. The framework is hypothesis-generating; prospective studies with standardised patellofemoral kinematic endpoints are required for validation.

paper_title: Reconstructing Complete 3D Humans from Limited Observations: A Survey
paper_abstract: Reconstructing a complete 3D human from the observations available in practice, such as a single photograph, an occluded video, a degraded archival image, or a personal photo collection spanning years, requires inferring content that the input does not reveal. Data-driven priors, ranging from statistical body models to large image, video, and 3D generative models, have made such inference increasingly feasible. The resulting literature, however, is divided between reconstruction and generation communities that use different assumptions, terminology, and evaluation protocols. This survey organizes the field around limited observation rather than around a particular input modality or 3D representation. We characterize limitations along four axes, namely spatial completeness, temporal completeness, observation quality, and observation coherence, and use posterior inference as an analytical lens to classify methods by how they compensate for missing evidence. The resulting taxonomy comprises six method families: template-constrained fitting, feature-aligned reconstruction, canonical-space temporal aggregation, generative-prior-guided optimization, feed-forward generative reconstruction, and conditional generation. For each family, we analyze its mechanism, representative methods, strengths, and failure modes, and we identify recurring patterns by which practical systems combine several families. We then examine the gap between reference-based evaluation and the assessment of plausible, uncertain completions. Finally, we discuss open challenges, including multi-hypothesis outputs, provenance of reconstructed content, fusion of unconstrained photo collections, degradation-aware inference, physical plausibility, and the emerging role of multimodal language models and agents.

paper_title: Prevalence and Associated Risk Factors of Hypertension and Pre-Hypertension Among the Adult Population: Findings from the Dubai Household Survey, 2024
paper_abstract: Objectives: This study aims to determine the prevalence of hypertension (HTN) and pre-hypertension (PHTN) among adults in Dubai, the United Arab Emirates. Furthermore, it seeks to identify the associated sociodemographic characteristics and cardiometabolic risk within this population. Methods: This investigation utilized data from the 2024 Dubai Household Health Survey (DHHS), a population-based cross-sectional study employing a multistage stratified cluster sampling methodology. Data on socio-demographic characteristics, behavioral risk factors, blood pressure measurements, anthropometric parameters, and blood glucose levels were collected from 2530 adult participants representing the population of Dubai. All analyses were conducted using R statistical software, incorporating survey analysis procedures to account for the complex sampling design. Results: The weighted prevalence of HTN was 36.9% (95% CI: 35.1–40.3), and PHTN was 32.2% (95% CI: 27.9–36.4) among adults aged ≥18 years in Dubai, indicating that 69.1% of the adult population had elevated blood pressure. HTN prevalence increased with age, was higher in males than females, and was more prevalent among non-nationals and those with lower educational attainment. Cardiometabolic risk factors such as high cholesterol (56.6% in HTN, 53.9% in PHTN) and obesity (26.9% in HTN, 20.6% in PHTN) were common in both groups, with diabetes being significantly higher in the HTN group (20.7% vs 11.8%). Conclusions: The study reveals a high burden of HTN and PHTN in Dubai's adult population, with significant associations with age, gender, nationality, education, and various cardiometabolic risk factors. These findings underscore the urgent need for targeted public health interventions and early detection strategies to mitigate the rising prevalence of elevated blood pressure and associated cardiovascular risks in Dubai, the UAE.

paper_title: AGI and Education 5.0: A Systematic Review of AGI-Driven Sustainable Education Across the Learning Lifespan
paper_abstract: Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) is increasingly envisioned as a transformative force in education, yet research on AGI-driven education remains fragmented across educational stages and rarely incorporates sustainability into system design and evaluation. This systematic review examines how AGI and large language model (LLM)/generative AI technologies reshape education across the learning lifespan and how sustainability can be embedded in AGI-powered education. Following PRISMA guidelines, we searched Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, and Google Scholar for studies published between 2015 and 2026, using keyword groups related to general intelligence, education, and sustainability. After screening, 85 peer-reviewed studies were included and synthesized through narrative synthesis. Given that full AGI remains unrealized, current LLM and generative AI systems are treated as emergent approximations of AGI’s educational potential. We develop an organizing framework that maps AGI’s transformative roles, key mechanisms, and sustainability implications across early childhood, K–12, higher education, and lifelong learning. The review identifies four emerging application scenarios and introduces a multidimensional sustainability lens encompassing cognitive, economic, social, and ethical–environmental dimensions, extending evaluation beyond conventional academic performance indicators. It also highlights persistent technical, social, and ethical challenges. By integrating stage-specific transformations with a lifespan and sustainability perspective, this review provides a reference and research agenda for the responsible and sustainable integration of AGI into Education 5.0.

paper_title: From Pixels to Actions: A Comprehensive Review of Spatiotemporal Understanding from Visual Perception to Vision-Language-Action Models
paper_abstract: Spatial intelligence, the ability to perceive, reconstruct, reason about, predict, and act within dynamic three-dimensional environments, is a unifying goal for robotics, autonomous driving, and embodied AI. Existing surveys treat its components, from video language models to Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, in isolation, obscuring how progress at one capability carries over to the next. This review provides a unified, critical analysis of the full pipeline from pixels to actions. We introduce the Pixels-to-Actions (P2A) hierarchy, a six-level taxonomy: (L1) visual perception, (L2) temporal perception, (L3) spatial and 4D understanding, (L4) spatiotemporal reasoning, (L5) predictive world modeling, and (L6) embodied action. For each level, we analyze architectures, spatiotemporal tokenization, multi-sensor inputs, and training paradigms. We examine whether stronger geometric grounding and temporal reasoning translate into better prediction and action, and formalize streaming spatial intelligence as a unifying target. We extend the analysis to medical imaging, remote sensing, AR/VR, surveillance, and digital twins, and compare datasets, benchmarks, and metrics from video question answering to closed-loop evaluation. We distill ten open problems, including weak spatial grounding in multimodal models, limited physical commonsense, costly long-horizon reasoning, fragmented benchmarks, and insufficient safety evaluation. A continuously updated repository of the reviewed literature is available at https://github.com/binayksingh/Awesome-Pixels-to-Actions.

paper_title: Literature Review on the Impact of COVID-19 on the Development of Sustainable and Resilient Tourism
paper_abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic catalyzed a reconfiguration of tourism, forcing its transition towards more resilient and sustainable paradigms. This literature review synthesizes current knowledge on this transformation, analyzing the conceptual evolution of sustainability, research trends, methodological limitations, and future lines of study. Findings indicate a redefinition of the concept integrating public health and equity, greater effectiveness of strategies such as diversification and proximity tourism, and the persistence of gaps such as scarce longitudinal data. It concludes by underscoring the need for interdisciplinary approaches, such as the circular economy and the “One Health” model, to establish a transformative and lasting recovery.

paper_title: Governance, Financing, and Service Delivery Challenges in Pakistan’s Healthcare System: A Critical Narrative Review
paper_abstract: In Pakistan, rapid population growth, financial constraints, and chronic underinvestment have weakened the public healthcare system. Following the 2010–2011 constitutional devolution, healthcare governance and financing were transferred to provincial governments through a three-tiered public network comprising primary, secondary, and tertiary facilities. This critical review analyzes structural issues and inter-provincial disparities following the devolution of authority, based on the WHO’s “Health System Building Blocks” framework. A total of 40 peer-reviewed studies and 7 official documents (n = 47) were examined. The findings reveal that despite the devolution of authority and the scaling back of social health protection programs such as Sehat Sahulat, Pakistan continues to lag behind South Asian benchmarks in maternal and child survival and public health investments. Public health expenditure stagnates at 0.8–0.9% of Gross Domestic Product (GDP), leaving out-of-pocket (OOP) payments at 52.93% of total health spending—more than triple the global average of 17.33%. Progress across the WHO’s six core building blocks is hindered by an imbalance between nurses and physicians (5.2 nurses per 10,000 population), a shortage of healthcare workers in rural areas, and fragmented pharmaceutical regulations. The District Health Information System (DHIS2) fails to integrate with other systems. Macro-fiscal constraints, such as low tax revenues, a heavy debt burden, and the channeling of resources toward treatment-focused hospitals, continue to weaken the state's capacity for implementation. To achieve Universal Health Coverage (UHC), priority must be given to primary healthcare services and public health policies. It is essential to restructure insurance packages through local health taxes, regulate informal healthcare providers at the provincial level, and institutionalize coordination between federal and provincial authorities.

paper_title: Personalized Digital Advertising and Consumer Privacy Concerns: An Integrative Review of Brand Trust and Purchase Intention
paper_abstract: Personalised digital advertising is likely to improve relevance and ease of search, but practices that support personalisation may also trigger concerns that consumers are being monitored, profiled, or exploited. This review explores the role of privacy concern in brand trust and purchase intention, attending to conditions that determine when personalisation might increase or decrease effectiveness. Based on a structured integrative review of peer-reviewed advertising, marketing, and information-systems literature, supplemented by official regulatory publications and institutional reporting, this review employs thematic synthesis to compare the evidence for relevance, intrusiveness, information-flow expectations, transparency, control, and trust. Across field experiments, scenario studies, representative surveys, and previous reviews, there is no consistent evidence to support a "more personalisation is better" rule. Personalisation enhances message effectiveness to the degree that content is useful, timely, or based on data that consumers would expect a firm to use. Personalisation decreases effectiveness if the data were inferred, or obtained surreptitiously, or if detailed information is perceived as intrusive, or if an explanation reveals an unacceptable volume of data flow. Information transparency and user control are therefore not automatic solutions to build trust, but rather conditional signals, reliant on whether the practices in question are deemed appropriate. Recent multi-national survey evidence further shows that, indeed, perceived privacy concern diminishes trust; however, trust and perceived usefulness appear to reliably increase purchase intention. This review produces a five-part, purpose-limited, relevance-based framework, linking data practices, consumer interpretation, brand trust, and purchase intention. Recommendations include purpose-limited, contextual, and consensual data use, empowering control, transparent practices, and evolving privacy by design strategies over indiscriminate or irreversible targeting. Given this is not a meta-analysis, no inferences are made regarding pooled effects.

paper_title: Gamification in the age of AI: surveying player perceptions of motivation, manipulation, and data protection
paper_abstract: Modern games and applications increasingly employ artificial intelligence (AI), user modeling, and gamification to influence user behavior, sustain engagement, and monetize attention. Although these mechanisms can enhance motivation and enjoyment, they also raise concerns about manipulation, personal data usage, and transparency. To examine how players perceive these dynamics, we conducted a survey with 28 adult participants. Respondents expressed strong concerns about the collection and exploitation of personal information in games and gamified applications, while also reporting low awareness and a limited sense of control over how their data is used. They evaluated progression features such as leveling systems and leaderboards as motivating. In contrast, they rated retention-focused mechanics such as daily login rewards and random reward reveals as highly manipulative. Participants reported that these systems can create fear of missing out or resemble gambling. Participants also expressed support for regulatory measures that limit exploitative design and protect vulnerable users. These findings reveal a clear gap between increasingly powerful engagement strategies and user trust, illustrating the need for more responsible and transparent gamification practices.

paper_title: A comprehensive survey of deep face verification systems adversarial attacks and defense strategies
paper_abstract: Face Verification (FV) systems have exhibited remarkable performance in verification tasks and have consequently garnered extensive adoption across various applications, from identity duplication to authentication in mobile payments. However, the surge in popularity of face verification has raised concerns about potential vulnerabilities in the face of adversarial attacks. These concerns originate from the fact that advanced FV systems, which rely on deep neural networks, have recently demonstrated susceptibility to crafted input samples known as adversarial examples. Although imperceptible to human observers, adversarial examples can deceive deep neural networks during the testing and deployment phases. These vulnerabilities raised significant concerns about the deployment of deep neural networks in safety-critical contexts, prompting extensive investigations into adversarial attacks and corresponding defense strategies. This comprehensive survey provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in deep face verification, encompassing a broad spectrum of topics such as algorithmic designs, database utilization, protocols, and application scenarios. Furthermore, we conduct an in-depth examination of state-of-the-art algorithms to generate adversarial examples and the defense mechanisms devised to mitigate such adversarial threats.

paper_title: Tejaswini Niranjana's Contribution to Postcolonial Translation Studies: A Critical Review
paper_abstract: The emergence of Postcolonial Translation Studies in the late twentieth century marked a significant shift in translation scholarship from linguistic concerns to questions of power, ideology, and cultural representation. Among the scholars who contributed to this transformation, Tejaswini Niranjana occupies a central position. Her seminal work, Siting Translation: History, Post-Structuralism, and the Colonial Context (1992), challenged traditional assumptions regarding the neutrality of translation and demonstrated how translation functioned as a discursive instrument in the construction and maintenance of colonial authority. This review article critically examines Niranjana's contribution to Postcolonial Translation Studies by analyzing her major theoretical interventions, intellectual influences, and lasting impact on contemporary translation scholarship. The discussion explores her critique of Western translation theories, her analysis of the relationship between translation and colonial discourse, and her conceptualization of translation as a political and ideological practice. The article further evaluates the strengths and limitations of her framework and considers its relevance to current developments in translation research, including audiovisual translation, cultural translation, and globalization studies. By reviewing three decades of scholarship influenced by Niranjana, the study argues that her work remains foundational for understanding translation as a site of cultural negotiation, identity formation, and power relations in postcolonial contexts.

paper_title: Return to Sport and Physical Activity After Hip Resurfacing Arthroplasty Versus Total Hip Arthroplasty in Young, Active Adults: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
paper_abstract: Background: Hip resurfacing arthroplasty (HRA) is widely believed to confer a greater capacity for high-level physical activity than total hip arthroplasty (THA) in young, active patients. However, the extent to which this apparent advantage reflects a true procedural effect, as opposed to preferential selection of more active patients for HRA, remains unclear.Methods: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis in accordance with PRISMA 2020, searching PubMed and Scopus for comparative studies reporting post-operative University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) activity scores in patients undergoing HRA versus THA. Pooled mean differences (MD) were estimated using a random-effects model (restricted maximum likelihood). Pre-specified subgroup analyses stratified studies by design (comparative versus non-comparative) and by whether baseline activity level was equalised between treatment arms at study entry.Results: Thirteen studies met inclusion criteria (1,327 hips; 644 HRA, 683 THA). Patients undergoing HRA achieved modestly higher post-operative activity scores than those undergoing THA (MD 0.75, 95% CI 0.35–1.14; p<0.001), a difference below the accepted minimal clinically important difference of one point. Heterogeneity was high (I²=78%). Study design category did not explain this heterogeneity (comparative versus non-comparative studies, p=0.69); however, baseline activity equalisation did: studies with unequal baseline activity reported more than double the effect size of those with equalised baselines (1.47 vs 0.51 points; p<0.001). No evidence of publication bias was detected (Egger's p=0.55; Begg's p=0.68).Discussion: The activity advantage attributed to hip resurfacing is small, clinically marginal, and appears substantially attributable to baseline selection of more active patients rather than a true procedural benefit. Future comparative studies of post-operative activity after hip arthroplasty should prospectively match or statistically adjust for baseline activity level to minimise confounding by indication.

paper_title: Functional Divergence of Upper- and Lower-Body Fat Distribution and Differences in Cardiovascular and Cerebrovascular Disease Risk and Outcomes: A Narrative Review
paper_abstract: Traditional obesity risk assessment centers on body mass index (BMI); however, marked differences in cardiovascular and cerebrovascular outcomes despite comparable total adiposity suggest that the regional attributes of adipose tissue have independent explanatory value. Consistent evidence from cohort studies and Mendelian randomization (MR) shows that upper-body (abdominal/truncal) fat is positively associated with cardiovascular and cerebrovascular risk, whereas lower-body (gluteofemoral/leg) fat is independently associated with reduced risk at the adipose depot volume level. In a South Indian dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) study, each 1-SD increase in android fat was associated with an odds ratio (OR) for type 2 diabetes of 6.59 (95% CI, 3.17–13.70) in men, whereas the OR for leg fat was 0.42 (95% CI, 0.24–0.74). A dose-response meta-analysis showed that each 10-cm increase in hip circumference was associated with a 10% lower risk of all-cause mortality (hazard ratio (HR), 0.90; 95% CI, 0.81–0.99); after adjustment for BMI and waist circumference, the association strengthened to an HR of 0.78 (95% CI, 0.66–0.90). Data from the UK Biobank showed that, after adjustment for BMI and waist circumference, each 1-SD increase in hip circumference was associated with a 5% lower risk of coronary heart disease (HR, 0.95; 95% CI, 0.93–0.97). A cross-cohort reclassification analysis showed that among individuals with a "normal-weight" BMI, 5% had an elevated waist circumference and 18% had an elevated waist-to-hip ratio; most of these individuals, who were not identified by BMI-based classification, had a 15%–50% increased risk of cardiovascular outcomes. A Chinese population cohort showed that dynamic changes in the weight-adjusted waist index were independently associated with cardiovascular and cerebrovascular mortality, with the group showing the largest increase having a 1.52-fold higher risk than the lowest group. Upper-body fat risk exhibited a dose-dependent pattern: a high visceral adiposity index was associated with a 55% increased risk of cardiovascular disease (risk ratio (RR), 1.55; 95% CI, 1.36–1.76). The causal signal for visceral adipose tissue (VAT) is highly sensitive to exposure definition and inferential framework. Within an MR framework using MRI-measured VAT volume and BMI adjustment, VAT had no robust effect on atherosclerotic outcomes. In contrast, observational associations of BMI-adjusted MRI-defined VAT showed a positive signal. An MR study across multiple vascular beds used MRI-derived fat depots as exposure measures. After BMI adjustment, each 1-SD increase in gluteofemoral adipose tissue (GFAT) volume was associated with 17%, 24%, and 28% lower risks of myocardial infarction, large-artery atherosclerotic stroke, and peripheral artery disease, respectively. These effects attenuated but remained significant after adjustment for lipids. In contrast, causal estimates for waist-to-hip ratio (WHR) and hip circumference were not robust in sensitivity analyses. Sex-specific MR showed that the causal association between WHR and coronary heart disease was significant in women (OR, 1.16; 95% CI, 1.06–1.26) but not in men. At the mechanistic level, paired chromatin landscape analysis of subcutaneous adipose tissue (SAT) and omental visceral adipose tissue (OVAT) showed that OVAT-specific differentially accessible regions were approximately twice as numerous as those in SAT and were enriched at promoters of cardiomyopathy-related genes. AI-driven large-scale clinical phenotyping in 101,243 patients showed that individuals positive for brown adipose tissue (BAT) had a lower prevalence of cardiovascular and psychiatric diseases. Higher BAT activity was associated with lower odds of cardiometabolic disease, and angiotensin receptor blocker use was positively associated with BAT, suggesting that BAT has preliminary druggable-target signals, although causal and hard-endpoint evidence is not yet established. A retrospective cohort of 13,530 patients undergoing PET/CT further showed that BAT positivity was independently associated with a lower incidence of cardiovascular events (P=0.018). Perivascular adipose tissue (PVAT) and epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) influence arterial stiffness, ventricular remodeling, and arrhythmias through paracrine pathways adjacent to target organs. EAT volume was independently associated with new-onset atrial fibrillation (HR per 1-SD increase, 1.29; 95% CI, 1.05–1.58; still significant after adjustment for BMI and left atrial volume). The CT-accessible Fat Attenuation Index has translated the inflammatory phenotype of PVAT into a clinically deployable prognostic tool; pericoronary adipose tissue (PCAT) attenuation was significantly associated with major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) risk (HR, 1.58; 95% CI, 1.38–1.81) and all-cause mortality (HR, 1.77), but this effect size was highly sensitive to analytical strategy. Radiomic quantification of EAT volume and the PVAT inflammatory phenotype jointly support the feasibility of opportunistic risk stratification. At the intervention level, several lines of evidence jointly support "distribution improvement" as an independent dimension for evaluating interventions beyond weight loss alone. These include CENTRAL/DIRECT-PLUS, the primary and mediation analyses of SELECT, comparisons of VAT reduction across different intervention pathways, the SUMMIT CMR substudy, the DAPA-EAT trial, and evidence on dapagliflozin and EAT. Heart failure outcomes exhibit heterogeneity by ejection fraction phenotype. A prospective cohort of 428,000 participants in the UK Biobank showed that heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) was independently associated with all adiposity measures (VAT: HR, 1.23), whereas heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) was not independently associated with adiposity measures. EAT was consistently associated with harm in HFpEF/heart failure with mildly reduced ejection fraction (HFmrEF) but showed a paradoxical association in HFrEF. Among patients with HFpEF, 91% had an elevated waist circumference and 85% had elevated VAT, but only 38% met the BMI criterion for obesity. The PARAGON-HF trial further showed that the prevalence of central obesity (waist-to-height ratio (WHtR) ≥0.5) in HFpEF was as high as 96%, whereas BMI-defined obesity was present in only 49%. In diabetic HFrEF, cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR)-defined sarcopenic obesity was independently associated with approximately a 3-fold risk of adverse outcomes (HR, 3.03; 95% CI, 1.39–6.63). Three-dimensional deep learning segmentation of whole-body MRI has enabled direct quantification of GFAT and provided incremental discrimination of ΔAUC 0.01–0.02 beyond models already containing BMI and WHR. A sarcopenic obesity index derived from routine CMR (body weight/pectoralis major mass) in 55,768 UK Biobank CMR scans showed that each 1-SD increase was associated with a 31% higher risk of incident heart failure, a 51% higher risk of cardiovascular death, and a 37% higher risk of all-cause death. This index provides a scalable operational tool for characterizing the "fat–muscle configuration." AI-derived MRI body composition analysis further showed that, after full adjustment for BMI and waist circumference, only VAT proportion and skeletal muscle fat fraction independently provided incremental prognostic information for MACE. This suggests that opportunistic radiomic quantification is extending beyond the boundaries of circumference-based proxies. Critical benchmarking of novel body shape indices suggests that BMI combined with WHR captures nearly all body shape information relevant to cardiometabolic disease; novel indices have incremental value but are not yet sufficient to support widespread replacement of BMI + WHR. The Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA) cohort showed that WHR significantly modifies the cardiovascular risk associated with lipoprotein(a) (Lp[a]): individuals with Lp(a) ≥50 mg/dL and WHR ≥90th percentile had the highest atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) incidence (35.7/1,000 person-years). The American Diabetes Association (ADA) 2026 standards and the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome guideline have incorporated distribution indicators such as waist circumference into risk stratification; the Expert Consensus on the Management of Obesity in the Elderly (2026 Edition) further provides diagnostic cutoffs for waist circumference and waist-to-hip ratio in Chinese older adults. This narrative review synthesizes the above evidence, using "functional divergence" as the organizing thread.

paper_title: Supply-Side Health System Determinants of Mental Healthcare Access for Black Canadians: A Scoping Review
paper_abstract: Background/Objectives: Improving access to mental healthcare for Black communities is a policy priority in Canada, yet existing reviews have focused largely on service users. This review aimed to identify supply-side barriers and facilitators to mental healthcare access for Black communities in Canada and to show where in the health system they occur. Methods: Following Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and PRISMA-ScR, MEDLINE, Embase, PsycINFO, CINAHL, and Scopus were searched from inception to 13 April 2026, with a complementary search on 9 August 2026. Two reviewers screened peer-reviewed empirical studies. Barriers and facilitators were charted under the six World Health Organization (WHO) health-system building blocks and analyzed using deductive–inductive qualitative content analysis. Results: Twenty-one studies were included, 14 of which used qualitative designs. Barriers were reported in every building block and were concentrated in service delivery and the health workforce. The most widely reported barriers were a lack of culturally appropriate services, long waits and distant care, and a lack of Black and culturally trained providers. Facilitators were reported less often and included provider–client concordance, community and peer-led services, culturally responsive practice, and holistic, faith-inclusive care. Health information systems, essential medicines and technologies, and health financing received the least attention. Conclusions: Barriers to mental healthcare for Black communities in Canada extend across the health system. Improving access will require a coordinated approach that strengthens the Black and culturally responsive workforce, invests in community-led services, and involves Black communities in leadership and decision-making.

paper_title: From AI-Assisted to Autonomous Cybersecurity: A Systematic Review
paper_abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is moving cybersecurity from rule-based and analyst-driven operations towards agentic and potentially autonomous cyber defence.
