The review finds that the enabling methods are mature in road-vehicle and laboratory contexts but that railway-specific validation, uncertainty-aware decision support, twin qualification criteria and demonstrated operational benefit are lacking in the literature examined. A prioritised research agenda is presented. The review is narrative rather than systematic; gaps are stated relative to the sources examined.

paper_title: Experimental Evidence for Effects of Chronic Infra-Sound Exposure on the Heart – A Narrative Review
paper_abstract: This narrative review outlines potential pathophysiological mechanisms in the mammalian heart in response to chronic infrasound exposure from technical installations. Recent research findings suggest that repeated exposure to infrasound can activate the heart's mechanosensitive PIEZO-1 channels. PIEZO-1 plays an important role in cardiac contractility via modulation of Ca²⁺ release and is involved in ROS homeostasis. The increasingly widespread sources of technical infrasound - which often exhibit high sound pressure intensities at infrasonic frequencies - should be reevaluated with regard to their impact on living organisms. Experimental overexpression of cardiac PIEZO-1 in mice serves as an example of potential effects of chronic infrasound exposure on the heart. Associated reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation reveals links to inflammatory pathways. Continued PIEZO-1 (over)stimulation appears to disrupt Ca²⁺ and ROS homeostasis in the long term, ultimately resulting in cardiomyopathy and arrhythmogenicity.

paper_title: Dimensional Assessment of Personality Pathology and Treatment Adaptation in Alcohol Use Disorder: From an Empty Systematic Review to a Narrative Synthesis
paper_abstract: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) and personality disorders (PD) co-occur in up to two thirds of treatment-seeking patients, and comorbidity predicts poorer engagement and relapse. Current diagnostic frameworks (DSM-5 Alternative Model, ICD-11, HiTOP) describe personality pathology dimensionally, which is expected to be less stigmatizing, more acceptable to patients and more useful for treatment planning. We aimed to identify programs that assess personality dimensionally in patients with AUD and adapt treatment to the profile obtained. Following a PROSPERO-registered protocol (CRD420260656442), PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus and Web of Science were searched (February–March 2025). Of 2,529 records, 72 were assessed in full text; none met the pre-specified criteria, so the review was converted into a narrative synthesis of the 44 closest reports plus one case report identified outside the search. Reports fell into three groups: dimensional assessment without consequences for treatment; treatment adapted to a categorical PD diagnosis (schema, psychodynamic or mentalization-based therapies) or transdiagnostic treatments that did not assess personality; and contextual evidence on comorbidity, typologies and assessment. The only near-miss relied on a categorical Millon inventory. We discuss why assessment and intervention remain disconnected and propose brief dimensional screening at treatment entry as a pathway to person-centered, less stigmatizing AUD care.

paper_title: Bambara Groundnut and Finger Millet for Instant Complementary Foods: A Narrative Critical Review of Molecular Composition, Processing-Induced Chemical Changes, Functionality and Sensory Quality
paper_abstract: Bambara groundnut (Vigna subterranea) and finger millet (Eleusine coracana) are underutilised African crops whose combination could improve the protein quality and micronutrient density of cereal-based instant complementary foods. This review examines the molecular constituents that determine their nutritional and technological value, as well as the chemical changes induced by processing. Bambara groundnut supplies lysine-rich protein and starch; nonetheless, its use is limited by phytic acid, phenolic compounds, a hard-to-cook defect linked to pectin–phytate interactions and cell wall lignification, and beany volatiles such as hexanal and 2-pentylfuran. Finger millet provides starch, calcium and phenolic acids, a large share of which are bound to cell wall polysaccharides, together with phytate and tannins that chelate minerals and bind proteins. Soaking, germination, fermentation and malting activate phytases and amylases, lowering phytate by up to 67% and finger millet paste viscosity from 1305 to 18 cP, while microwave and infrared heating gelatinise starch, aggregate proteins and shorten cooking time. Evidence for a finished product is limited to one instant porridge reported in a doctoral thesis. Future studies should link processing conditions to molecular outcomes, including phenolic and phytate profiles, starch and protein structure, volatile composition and in vitro digestibility, in a reconstituted Bambara groundnut–finger millet porridge

paper_title: NEXUSFlow: A Multi-Boat Autonomous Survey System for Locating Bank-Side Arsenic Sources in Rivers—System Design and Monte Carlo Evaluation
paper_abstract: Arsenic contamination of the Kok River in northern Thailand is currently monitored by manual sampling at fixed points, and laboratory results take three to four weeks, while the source often remains unknown. We present NEXUSFlow, a monitoring system in which a fleet of five autonomous surface vehicles surveys a river reach along automatically planned zigzag routes, a plume-mapping model (PatternTrack AI) estimates the contaminant field and traces its source, and an AI agent (NATEE) drafts a response plan that is released only after approval by a pollution control officer and a village leader. To test the central design choice—mobile zigzag sampling instead of fixed stations—we ran a Monte Carlo simulation of 2,000 bank-side discharges in a 12 km reach using a two-dimensional transverse-mixing model with reflecting banks. The median full-mixing length was 46 km, so plumes remained attached to one bank throughout the reach. In the 1,776 scenarios in which some location exceeded 0.01 mg/L, seven fixed stations on one bank detected the plume in 38% of cases, stations on both banks in 75%, mid-channel stations in 2% and a centreline boat in 4%, whereas a 40-sample zigzag survey detected 83%. A short follow-up along the affected bank reduced the median source-location error to 15 m, compared with about 830 m for fixed stations. The ranking was unchanged for strongly meandering reaches. A prototype run on simulated data took 81 min from the first report to a village alert. The results support combining mobile zigzag surveys with fixed stations and must be confirmed by field tests.

paper_title: Deep-Learning Prediction of Reversed-Phase Liquid Chromatographic Retention Times for Small Molecules and Pharmaceuticals: A Systematic Review
paper_abstract: Predicted retention times can narrow candidate lists in liquid chromatography–high-resolution mass spectrometry (LC–HRMS). Deep-learning models report errors near the variability between repeated measurements, but their credibility depends on the evaluation design. We reviewed deep-learning retention-time prediction for non-polymeric small molecules in reversed-phase liquid chromatography (RP-LC). Searches of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science through August 3, 2026, identified 594 records; 33 studies were eligible. Fifteen studies reported mean absolute errors (MAEs) on the METLIN Small Molecule Retention Time (SMRT) dataset across at least seven differently filtered subsets. Among 13 models evaluated under a broad retained-only convention, the spread from best to worst was 18 s, compared to the 36 s mean repeat-measurement variability observed on SMRT reference standards. Unseen chromatographic methods were rarely tested; one model’s error rose from 29.3 s internally to 596.8 s on a held-out gradient. Random molecular partitions remained common, including in studies using cross-validation or transfer-set deduplication. Risk of bias was low in 18 studies for model development and 19 for performance evaluation, but in only seven for leakage control and one for generalizability. Reported accuracy depends as much on benchmark construction as on architecture. To support reliable compound identification, these models need structure-aware and method-aware validation with uncertainty estimates.

paper_title: Water-Damaged Buildings and Health: An Updated Review of the Evidence, Sources of Bias, and Co-Occurring Conditions
paper_abstract: Background. Water damage in buildings produces a mixture that includes fungi, bacteria, endotoxin, microbial fragments, and moisture-driven chemical emissions. The respiratory evidence has been graded; evidence on the multisystem symptoms many people report has been graded limited or inadequate, or not graded. Objectives. To summarize the evidence as of 2026; to examine how confounding, reporting bias, the composition of the exposure mixture, and co-occurring clinical conditions bear on the observed associations; and to propose a protocol for a rigorous future review. Methods. Structured evidence review (PubMed, Europe PMC, agency sources) with structured supplementary searches by body system and by exposure agent in November 2026 (145 database strategies); no registered protocol or duplicate screening. Results. The IOM and WHO graded no outcome as causal; two later reviews judged the evidence causal for asthma exacerbation in children, whereas a 2024 GRADE review rated effects in people with asthma uncertain. Pooled respiratory odds ratios are about 1.3 to 1.8, smaller in cohorts, and change modestly with socioeconomic adjustment. Measured agents such as endotoxin show both adverse and inverse associations. No epidemiological study of metabolic, hepatic, renal, endocrine, cardiovascular, or cancer outcomes, or of occupants' gut microbiome, was identified; these gaps indicate neither presence nor absence of an effect. No identified study systematically screened exposed people for bile acid malabsorption, iron deficiency, thyroid disease, sleep apnea, perimenopause, celiac disease, or postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome. HLA-DR typing has not been shown to provide diagnostic information. Conclusions. The respiratory and allergic evidence is sufficient to establish association. Beyond the airway, associations are reported for mental health, general symptoms, child neurodevelopment, skin, immune markers, and sarcoidosis, mostly in cross-sectional and self-reported designs; for metabolic, hepatic, renal, endocrine, cardiovascular, and cancer outcomes no epidemiological study was identified. The studies that would establish or exclude these associations have not been carried out, and tests used to assess exposure and susceptibility in an individual have not been validated for that purpose. The review sets out the design that research capable of answering these questions would require.

paper_title: The Daydreaming Factory: A Twin-Calibrated Simulation Framework for Proactive Reliability Exploration of Battery-Powered Rail Vehicles—A Critical Review and Research Agenda
paper_abstract: Battery-powered and electric rail vehicles move substantial dependability risk onto battery systems, thermal management, power electronics and software for which no mature fleet failure history exists. Conventional reliability methods depend on failure modes identified beforehand and calibrated by field experience that is not yet available. This critical review examines how twin-calibrated simulation can be used to explore failure possibilities proactively. The “Daydreaming Factory” a conceptual construct proposed here, not an established term is positioned against computational ideas of model-based imagination and is organised through three analytical devices: a taxonomy of virtual environments for reliability engineering, a causal-chain test from environment to reliability outcome, and a five-level evidence-maturity scale. The enabling methods are reviewed: multi-domain co-simulation, scenario generation and rare-event search, fault injection, degradation integration, and verification, validation and uncertainty quantification. A six-component reference framework with an explicit credibility layer is specified. Assessed against the sources examined, the individual methods are mature in adjacent domains, but integrated railway-specific implementations, field validation, qualification pathways and measured reliability benefits are largely absent. A research agenda and candidate performance indicators are proposed. The review is narrative rather than systematic and the framework has not been experimentally validated.

paper_title: Same Papers, Different Verdicts: Tracing Version Drift in LLM Peer Review
paper_abstract: Venues and benchmarks read LLM review scores as measurements of a paper, while providers replace their models within months. We audit twenty frontier models from OpenAI, Google and Anthropic on ICLR 2027 submissions while they were under review, with tests registered before the decisions. Between an earlier and a later version of Claude Opus and of Gemini, the share of papers placed on the accept side falls by 52 and 53 percentage points on 183 and 60 randomly drawn submissions, and by 43 to 79 points in six further paired comparisons, with no paper moving up in any of them. Stating a 30% acceptance rate in the prompt leaves a gap of 79 points between the two Opus versions. When score-stripped critiques are swapped between versions, the later critiques alone lower the accept share by 35 points for Opus and 51 for Gemini; for Opus the drop is 35 points under a third-party scorer and 24 after a rewrite that keeps each technical point and removes evaluative wording. On 57 papers, the percentiles of Opus 4.6 and 5.5 correlate at 0.73 while their accept shares differ by 44 points. On 99 to 119 submissions, the self-estimated percentiles of three models correlate with two human reviewers more strongly than a third reviewer does (point estimates 0.17 to 0.21, 95% intervals between -0.04 and +0.42). All twenty models give a 2 or a 3 in 473 of their 475 reviews, against 60 of 72 human reviews. Retrospective tests on decided papers can draw on memory. Claude Opus 5.5 names the true first author of 27 decided ICLR 2026 papers from their titles alone, with no wrong name, and Claude Opus 4.6 accepted all 11 decided papers it said it recognized, against 5 expected. Thresholds on LLM-reviewer scores therefore have to be validated against human decisions for each model version; our tests against the ICLR 2027 decisions follow on 16 December 2026.
comments: 19 pages, 5 figures. Results of the registered tests that need the ICLR 2027 decisions will be added after 16 December 2026

paper_title: Partitioning and Merging in Phase Unwrapping: A Systematic Review of Methods and Evidence
paper_abstract: Phase unwrapping underlies radar interferometry, magnetic resonance imaging and optical metrology. When an image is too large or too difficult to unwrap in one piece, many methods cut it into units, unwrap each unit, and merge the results. To our knowledge, no systematic review had brought these partitioned methods together. This review gathers them, for two-dimensional images and three-dimensional volumes. It describes how the units are built: fixed tiles, adaptive tiles, regions computed from the data, or pieces imposed by the acquisition, such as subapertures, slices and scenes. It then classifies how the units are merged, in four classes: after each unit is unwrapped, through one integer per jump-free region, during the solve, or through an external reference. Three findings stand out: building the units and merging them are two separate decisions; the merging rule decides whether the merged phase stays congruent with the measured one; and most tests change both decisions at once, so few results show which one helps. We state what a study can report to support a claim on memory, speed or accuracy. Our aim is to document the methods, not to rank them. Following PRISMA 2020, four bibliographic databases (OpenAlex, IEEE Xplore, Web of Science and Scopus), searched on 1 October 2026, returned 1,800 records. After removing duplicates, screening titles and abstracts, adding a citation search and reading 298 full texts, we included 149 studies, published from 1987 to 2026. The review was not registered and received no specific funding.

paper_title: Multimodal AI in Healthcare: Review of Vision-Language Foundation Models for Real-World Medical Applications
paper_abstract: The emergence of foundation models has marked a transformative shift in AI, enabling robust generalization across diverse downstream tasks through putative zero-shot learning. Large Language Models and Vision Language Models have demonstrated strong capabilities in tasks such as image interpretation, report generation, and question answering by effectively learning from multimodal data-images paired with associated text often with minimal supervision. In the healthcare domain, this ability to align visual and textual information reduces the reliance on extensive manual annotations, as models can leverage existing clinical reports and imaging data to learn meaningful representations. This integration holds promise for improving diagnostic support, treatment planning, and overall patient care, even in data constrained settings. In this review, we provide a definitive taxonomy of the medical VLM landscape, tracing the evolution from early Contrastive Alignment and Generative MLLMs to the cutting edge frontiers of Dense Pixel Grounding, Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE), and Reasoning Incentivized (RL) architectures. We critically examine the "medical bottleneck" identifying the persistent challenges of data scarcity, the "hallucination" risks in generative diagnostics, the computational strain of 3D volumetric processing, and the lack of standardized, clinically grounded evaluation metrics.

paper_title: Large Language Model-based Optimization for Wireless Communication: A Survey
paper_abstract: The growing complexity and dynamism of modern wireless communication frameworks have made real-time optimization essential for efficient resource allocation. Traditional optimization and machine-learning techniques often struggle with generalization, adaptability, stability, and scalability in heterogeneous, time-varying environments. Large language models (LLMs) have recently emerged as powerful tools capable of reasoning over structured prompts and generating context-aware decisions in real time without domain-specific retraining. This survey provides a comprehensive review of LLM-driven optimization techniques applied to wireless communication problems such as power control, bandwidth allocation, task offloading, and intelligent surface configuration. We introduce a functional taxonomy of LLM-enabled wireless resource management strategies and analyze the prompt engineering methodologies employed in recent literature. Furthermore, we develop a generalized analytical framework that categorizes LLM-based optimization architectures, including direct solution generation, closed-loop optimization with external verifiers, and representation encoding within trainable neural pipelines. To demonstrate practical applicability, we present representative case studies on LLM-assisted beam prediction for millimeter-wave systems and adaptive wireless resource allocation. Finally, we discuss emerging hybrid AI approaches for wireless networks.

paper_title: RTLReviewBench: LLM Hardware Reviewers Rarely Miss Bugs but Routinely Reject Correct RTL
paper_abstract: Hardware teams increasingly ask large language models (LLMs) to review register-transfer level (RTL) code, yet it is unclear whether a model can tell a correct module from a buggy one without simulating it. We introduce RTLReviewBench, a benchmark of 114 matched pairs of buggy and correct Verilog modules. Each pair shares one specification, most buggy modules are real failures of LLM code generators, and every label is confirmed by simulation. Evaluating 12 commercial and open-weight models, we find a consistent asymmetry: reviewers rarely accept buggy code but often reject correct code, producing more than five false rejections for every missed bug. Synthetic mutants hide part of the problem: on the same designs, models miss far fewer injected bugs than real ones. Asking a model to reason before it commits to a verdict sharply reduces false rejections for weaker reviewers, and a controlled ablation shows that where the reasoning appears in the output matters more than the instruction to reason, whereas sampling and majority voting do not help. A blinded audit further shows that some correct "buggy" verdicts rest on false technical claims. We release the benchmark, a harder split for future models, all model responses, and the evaluation code at https://github.com/yasirmahmud/RTLReviewBench
comments: 24 pages, 6 figures, 16 tables. Benchmark, model responses, and code: https://github.com/yasirmahmud/RTLReviewBench

paper_title: SurveyWeave: An Agentic Framework for Automated Survey Generation
paper_abstract: Surveys help researchers keep up with fast-moving fields, but they take weeks to months to write. Automated survey generation (AutoSurvey) can alleviate this situation, but it is challenging to draw on hundreds to thousands of precisely scoped papers, choose among many valid structures, and stay faithful to its sources while offering insights. We present SurveyWeave, an agentic architecture that decomposes the problem into four tasks coordinated by three agents, each reviewing others' work and conducting revisions based on feedback. We also introduce WeaveEval, a five-dimension evaluation grounded in prior surveys. A comprehensive comparison shows that SurveyWeave outperforms Codex by 8 points and the strongest AutoSurvey baseline by 6 points.

paper_title: Continuous-Space Diffusion and Flow Language Models: A Survey
paper_abstract: Continuous-space diffusion and flow language models generate text by updating real-valued vectors (such as token embeddings, compressed codes, or sentence vectors) and decoding them into discrete words at readout. We organize this literature by three coupled choices: the continuous state being refined, the transition operator that updates it, and the text interface that converts states into tokens. Because language is discrete while the state space is continuous, adapting image diffusion to text encounters rounding ambiguity and embedding collapse under squared-error regression, uninformative noise schedules, distribution shift between clean-text codecs and learned priors, and mode averaging in few-step sampling. Across published comparisons with autoregressive and discrete-diffusion baselines, continuous models show no general advantage over same-scale autoregressive models on open-ended text; the closest prompt-continuation tie uses different training sequence lengths and separately tuned samplers. RePlaid matches or improves upon masked diffusion in likelihood bounds past compute-optimal budgets, and large-scale blockwise adaptation brings continuous models close to masked baselines on mathematical reasoning and code; however, continuous models still trail autoregressive baselines in held-out likelihood bounds, and scaling fits indicate that matching exact autoregressive negative log-likelihood requires substantially more training compute. Their clearest gains over autoregressive decoding appear in gradient-guided control, plan-level diversity, and task-specific reasoning after targeted fine-tuning. Under few-step budgets, trajectory-consistent distillation and stochastic bridges prevent entropy collapse, yet no standalone continuous generator has shown an end-to-end latency win over optimized autoregressive decoding at matched quality; the reported matched-quality latency gains rely on autoregressive verification of continuous drafts. We close with open problems in likelihood scaling, readout fidelity, few-step serving, representation reuse, and post-training. Project Page: https://github.com/TokenRhythm/awesome-cdllm.

paper_title: Vision-Language-Action Models: A Life-Cycle Survey of Design, Training and Deployment
paper_abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models adapt web-pretrained vision-language models to output robot actions, so that web knowledge carries over to physical control. In under four years the field has grown from RT-2, the first VLA, to open models that fine-tune on a single consumer GPU and proprietary generalists that clean unseen homes. VLA research joins robotics, computer vision and language modelling, so this survey is written for researchers and practitioners from each of these fields. It reviews 89 works from December 2022 to October 2026, mainly on manipulation and navigation, plus humanoid control, world-action models and evaluation. Seven design axes follow a VLA's life cycle: model design (inputs and memory, architecture, action output, intermediate predictions), training (pretraining data, post-training) and deployment (real-time execution). We compare 22 models on these axes, with their training data, model size, inference speed and hardware. Three trends emerge. (i) Training data has broadened beyond teleoperated robot data (about 10,000 hours for $π_0$) to community-collected episodes and egocentric human video (20,000 hours for GR00T N1.7). (ii) Model sizes have split into two groups: most recent models have 3-7 billion parameters; a new group under one billion runs on consumer GPUs. (iii) Generalist VLAs handling both manipulation and navigation are emerging, such as UniVLA and Qwen-VLA. We also compare VLAs with world-action models, which predict future observations as well as actions, and review evidence that some VLAs with near-perfect benchmark scores fail after small scene changes. A practitioner's guide gives a default for each design decision, and a glossary supports readers new to the field.

paper_title: Agentic Artificial Intelligence in Forestry: A Survey of Its Development, Applications, Current Opinions and Future Directions
paper_abstract: Software has supported forest management decisions since the 1970s, from growth simulators to reinforcement learning. Since 2023, large language models (LLMs) have been combined with tools, retrieval, memory and planning to form artificial intelligence (AI) agents that analyse forest data, decide on a sequence of steps, and either advise a person or act through software and machines. This survey reviews agentic AI in forestry. It traces the development of agent concepts in the field, describes the components that current agentic systems share, and reviews applications in seven areas, from forest inventory to biodiversity monitoring. We found only 13 LLM-based agentic systems in forestry. Most are single LLM agents or small groups of role-based agents that coordinate perception models, geospatial databases and retrieval over documents. Their evaluation relies on case studies, small expert panels and public datasets, and none of the reviewed LLM-based agents controls forest machines in the field. Recurring problems are factual errors, weak spatial reasoning, missing connectivity in forests, the cybersecurity of connected machines and trust, and current evaluations are short compared with the decades over which forest decisions take effect. We derive research directions on evaluation with forest simulators, edge deployment, interoperability, graded human oversight and safety constraints for forest machines. A comparison with agriculture identifies designs that can be transferred, and we expect agents to become routine first in analysis and advice, then in planning with forest models, and only later in the supervision of forest machines.

paper_title: A Mixed-Method Assessment of Environmental Accessibility in Canadian Office Spaces: A Triangulation of IAQ Testing, Occupant Health Surveys, Scent-Free Policy Implementation, and Lived Experience
paper_abstract: With individuals spending approximately 90% of their time indoors, indoor air quality (IAQ) is a critical public health and environmental accessibility concern. Fragranced consumer products emit volatile organic compounds (VOCs), potentially creating barriers for individuals with multiple chemical sensitivity (MCS) and other health vulnerabilities. This convergent mixed-methods study integrated five evidence streams: IAQ measurements, occupant surveys, scent-free policy assessments, product emissions testing, and focus groups to examine chemical exposures and environmental accessibility in Canadian offices. Findings indicated substantial contributions from indoor VOC sources. Despite greater mechanical ventilation, non-scent-free environments exhibited higher VOC concentrations and indoor/outdoor ratios, emphasizing source control alongside ventilation. Scent-free environments generally had lower VOC concentrations, although residual exposures persisted. Overlapping VOCs detected in indoor air and consumer products, alongside policy implementation gaps, highlighted ongoing exposure prevention challenges. Occupants of scent-free workplaces reported more symptoms and chronic conditions, potentially reflecting greater reliance on these environments among vulnerable individuals. Focus-group findings further identified persistent accessibility barriers and challenges with policy implementation. Overall, findings support integrated strategies combining scent-free policies, low-emission product procurement, transparent labelling, effective source control, adequate ventilation, and consistent implementation to reduce chemical exposures and advance environmental accessibility in workplaces.

paper_title: Generative Artificial Intelligence in Judicial Processes: A Socio-Technical Scoping Review of Architectures, Tasks, and Institutional Risks (2023–Mid-2026)
paper_abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly used in legal research, litigation support, and judicial administration. This scoping review maps architectures, court-facing tasks, evaluation designs, and institutional risks in research on GenAI and large language models (LLMs). Framed by Joanna Briggs Institute guidance and reported with PRISMA-ScR, it screened 1,518 Scopus and Web of Science records (31 March 2026) and 1,000 supplementary Elicit results (July 2026) for publications from 2023 onward, which yielded 201 references. We then reassessed each reference against explicit GenAI and judicial relevance criteria in an AI-assisted workflow checked by one author, with a second screening by a different LLM, and recorded the decisions and reasons. We charted publication characteristics and primary evidence designs and checked selected outcomes against the original publications. The synthesis includes 189 publications. We retained 10 references for context and excluded 2. Offline model evaluations accounted for 106 publications (56.1%). Studies reported task-specific results for retrieval, summarization, prediction, and drafting. One audit of three commercial legal research tools found hallucinations in 17–33% of evaluated queries. The mapped evidence is consistent with source-grounded, reviewable assistance for defined tasks. Heterogeneous evaluations and limited evidence from operating courts constrain conclusions about routine judicial use.

paper_title: K-Pop Fandom and Parasocial Relationships Across Cultural Contexts: A Text-Mining Review of Emotional Attachment and Social Identity from a Cultural Psychology Perspective
paper_abstract: Research on K-pop fandom has grown rapidly, yet its literature on parasocial relationships, emotional attachment and social identity is dispersed across psychology, communication, marketing and tourism studies, which makes it hard to see what has been studied and how it is framed. This review applies text mining to a purposive corpus of 245 scholarly records on K-pop fandom and parasocial relationships, drawn from the reference list of this manuscript and not from a systematic database search. The scope is research on K-pop fans in any country; the review asks how the literature is framed, how often South Korea is named as a setting, and which topics key studies address on platforms, fan communities and local cultural contexts. Record titles and venues were analysed with term and n-gram frequencies, a ten-theme dictionary compared across three publication periods, non-negative matrix factorisation (NMF) topic modelling and a term co-occurrence network. These results describe how records are titled and grouped; they are not findings about fans. In this corpus, 70% of dated records appeared in 2024–2026 and journal articles make up 66%. Consumption and marketing (n = 75) and parasocial interaction (n = 59) are the most prevalent themes. Six topics and four network communities emerged (modularity = 0.34); terms for attachment and purchase intention co-occur in titles, but the relationship between these constructs can only be assessed from the studies themselves. South Korea is named in only a few titles or venues, whereas Indonesia is named most often, although study settings were not verified from abstracts or full texts. A narrative overview of key studies identifies research on platform-mediated intimacy, on fan communities as sites of both belonging and strain, and on local cultural contexts; individual study findings and settings were not verified against abstracts or full texts. We outline a research agenda for comparative, culturally grounded studies, including verified studies of Korean domestic fans.

paper_title: A Systematic Review of Planning and Routing Strategies for UAV-Based Search and Rescue Operations: Methods, Evidence, and Research Gaps
paper_abstract: This paper reports a systematic literature review of planning and routing strategies for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in search and rescue (SAR). The review followed a documented protocol and is reported according to PRISMA 2020 and PRISMA-S. From 3,642 database records and 96 titles from exploratory searches and the research group's collection, 54 studies were assessed in full text, and 46 primary studies published from 2021 to 2026 were included. Each study was classified by its presence model, detection model, and objective, and by route structure, revisiting, energy, coordination, risk, and validation. Quality, risk of bias, and level of evidence were also assessed. Coverage routing is the largest strategy family (16 studies), and metaheuristics are the most common method class (13). Risk of bias is high in 26 studies, 23 studies are purely synthetic, and only three flew real aircraft. Eight studies build a cell-wise presence map but treat detection as certain, only two calibrate detection against empirical data, and no study places ground risk in the cost of travel. Seventeen studies report an optimality reference, but only six extend it to the application scale. A pooled effect cannot be computed, so 52 observations from 31 studies are synthesized by stratum. Of twelve tracked gaps, seven were narrowed, four were confirmed, and one was maintained. The main gap is the combination of modeling elements. The median study meets three of nine tracked requirements, and the closest study meets eight but keeps closed routes and unbounded revisiting. No multi-vehicle routing formulation has had its predicted detection probability compared with field measurements. This extended version reports the complete protocol and the per-study classifications.

paper_title: Forty Years of The Legend of Zelda: A Scoping Review of Game Design, Computation, Culture, and Play
paper_abstract: Over four decades, The Legend of Zelda has evolved from a landmark action-adventure series into a recurring object of research across game studies, computer science, musicology, cultural studies, psychology, education, and related fields. This article presents a scoping review and structured survey of Zelda-related research across the franchise’s 1986–2026 history, examining how the series has been studied as a designed system, cultural artifact, interactive narrative, audiovisual environment, player-community object, and computational testbed. Following a PRISMA-ScR-informed process with duplicate screening and full-text eligibility assessment, 93 studies were included in the final synthesis: 52 Core scholarly studies, 40 complementary scholarly/grey-literature studies, and one complementary critical/industry record. The literature is strongly recent and unevenly distributed: 65 included studies were published from 2020 onward, while 44 explicitly address either Ocarina of Time or Breath of the Wild. Narrative and worldbuilding constitute the largest thematic area, whereas technology remains comparatively underrepresented as a primary research topic. In contrast, Zelda dungeon structures have become established computational objects for procedural content generation, formal modeling, and mixed-initiative design research. A sensitivity analysis restricted to the 52-study Core scholarly corpus preserved the principal distributional patterns, indicating that the main mapping conclusions are not driven by complementary evidence. Across the reviewed traditions, a recurring pattern is the interaction among spatial design, player agency, audiovisual feedback, narrative, and increasingly interoperable game systems. The survey identifies gaps in longitudinal analysis, technical research, visual studies, localization, empirical player research, and computational models of modern three-dimensional Zelda environments, positioning the franchise as a distinctive longitudinal case for studying the relationships among game design, technology, culture, computation, and play.

paper_title: Mass and Charge Transport Modeling, Multiphysics Analysis, and Architectural Optimization in Electrochemical Batteries: A Comprehensive Review
paper_abstract: The rapid escalation of global decarbonization demands electrochemical energy storage systems that balance high energy density, superior rate capability, and decadal operational reliability. However, academic research has disproportionately focused on cell-level "specific capacity" records under idealized laboratory testing, obscuring the decisive governing role of macroscopic mass and charge transport architectures during scale-up. In this review, we formulate an interpretable physical framework that systematically classifies electrochemical batteries into four fundamental transport architectures: (1) enclosed stacked architectures, (2) Pure Liquid-Flow architectures, (3) fuel cells with the continuous-flow electrocatalytic reactor architectures, and (4) cross-phase hybrid architectures. We comprehensively evaluate how transport boundary conditions dictate electrochemical performance across the representative stacked systems (including high-nickel ternary, LMFP, solid-state, sodium-ion, aqueous zinc, and dual-ion batteries) and the true flow systems (ranging from all-vanadium, all-iron, polysulfide-iodide, to aqueous organic redox chemistries). Furthermore, we provide a unified taxonomy of hybrid systems spanning gas–solid (metal–air), liquid–solid (zinc–bromine, zinc–iodine, slurry flow), and gas–liquid (hydrogen–halogen, hydrogen–iron) configurations, explicitly demonstrating why hybrid configurations that superficially stitch disparate features inevitably inherit the transport liabilities and interfacial failure modes of both constituent architectures. Most critically, to address the core scope of battery performance modeling, we introduce a rigorous four-level multiphysics modeling framework spanning: (Level 1) geometric effective transport and through-plane ohmic resistance scaling, establishing a transparent and fully reproducible 35 mV IR-scale baseline for 100 μm thick electrodes; (Level 2) transient solid-state diffusion truncation and Sand's time interfacial electrodeposition instability modeling, physically justifying the ~10 mA cm-2 rate ceiling in high-loading stacked cells; (Level 3) hydrodynamic convective mass transfer and parasitic shunt-current network modeling in flow manifolds; and (Level 4) multiphase reaction-diffusion and electrocrystallization coupling dynamics. By bridging microscopic pore-scale transport dynamics and system-level architectural modeling, this review provides a quantitative roadmap for diagnosing transport limitations and guiding the rational design of scalable electrochemical batteries.

paper_title: Collective Social Behaviours of AI Agents: A Survey of Causes, Effects, and Interventions
paper_abstract: Multiple AI agents, most of them built on large language models (LLMs), are collectively deployed to complete certain tasks. Their interactions produce collective behaviours known from human societies, such as conformity, polarisation, echo chambers, and capture by zealots. These collective behaviours cannot be fully predicted or observed by studying single agents alone. In this tutorial and survey paper, we discuss thirty-three behaviours and classify them as observed, emerging, or anticipated. Nineteen major observed behaviours are reviewed in six families, namely agreement, division, minority influence and manipulation, contagion and diffusion, cooperation and coordination, and structure and hierarchy. We review the causes, effects, and interventions of each. Interventions suppress a behaviour when its effects are harmful and promote it when its effects are beneficial. We also give examples to explain key models. A synthesis section summarises the drivers and interventions shared across families and presents a perspective on the fourteen remaining behaviours, which are either recently observed, emerging, or anticipated. Emerging and anticipated behaviours can affect the stability of societies and financial markets when LLM agents become prevalent. Moreover, we present a case study with a scalar model showing that similarity-based memory retrieval acts as an endogenous confidence bound. This retrieval can produce echo chambers among simulated agents with no network homophily. Also, we evaluate diversity-aware retrieval as an intervention. Finally, we discuss open research directions. The paper is multidisciplinary, bridging the humanities and social sciences, the study of social networks, and AI.

paper_title: Sleep and Gastric Myoelectrical Activity: A Scoping Review
paper_abstract: Sleep disturbance is common in disorders of the gut-brain interaction, and many patients with gastrointestinal diseases report symptom associations with sleep. Yet, how gastric myoelectrical activity varies across sleep remains poorly characterised. This scoping review mapped the evidence on sleep and gastric myoelectrical activities in healthy and clinical adult populations, and evaluated the methods used for overnight gastric monitoring. Following PRISMA-ScR guidelines and JBI methodology, three databases were searched in October 2026 for studies published from 1996 that analysed gastric myoelectrical activity in relation to sleep. Six studies were included, all using cutaneous electrogastrography. Two studies analysed gastric activity by polysomnography-resolved sleep stage, whereas four compared samples of gastric activity during sleep with waking periods. No two studies quantified gastric activity in the same way. Slow-wave magnitude was lower during sleep in every study that assessed it, whereas slow-wave rate was largely preserved. Slow-wave rhythm tended to become less regular, with less time spent in normogastria, although findings were not consistent. In clinical populations, modulation of gastric activity appeared altered, though these were diverse and patterns differed between them. Sleep appears to be associated with changes in gastric myoelectrical activity, most consistently a decrease in slow-wave magnitude. However, the evidence base is small, methodologically heterogeneous, and reliant on recording modalities of limited reliability. Moreover, no study has characterised how gastric activity changes across the night. High-resolution recording of gastric myoelectrical activity is needed to form a more comprehensive understanding of nocturnal gastric physiology.

paper_title: Screening and Application of Starter Cultures in Traditional African Fermented Dairy Products (Lait caillé, Nono, Pendidam): A Review
paper_abstract: Raw milk is an essential food resource in Africa, but its preservation is hampered by the lack of a cold chain and by ambient temperatures generally exceeding 25-30 °C. Traditional fermentation practices give rise to iconic products such as Lait caillé (Senegal), Nono (Nigeria, Ghana) and Pendidam (Cameroon). Based on a literature search following the PRISMA 2020 recommendations, this review analyzes the physicochemical, microbiological and sensory characteristics of these products, the screening of potential starter cultures or probiotics, and their application to improve product quality. Lactic acid bacteria and some yeasts, including Saccharomyces cerevisiae, play a central role in indigenous fermentations, contributing to acidification, flavor and texture. The dominant lactic acid bacteria include Lactiplantibacillus plantarum, Lactococcus lactis and Leuconostoc mesenteroides in Lait caillé; Lactobacillus helveticus, Limosilactobacillus fermentum and Streptococcus thermophilus in Nono; and Lactobacillus spp. and Streptococcus spp. in Pendidam. A starter consortium combining an indigenous Lactobacillus rhamnosus isolate with extraneous cultures (Lactiplantibacillus plantarum, Lacticaseibacillus casei and Lactococcus lactis) for Nono production, and the probiotic L. rhamnosus yoba 2012 in Lait caillé, illustrate promising prospects for valorizing African milk. Such initiatives could broaden the commercialization of African fermented milks and justify further research on indigenous starters and probiotics, combined with good manufacturing practices.

paper_title: From Large Language Models (LLMs) to Agentic AI for IoT Security: A Survey
paper_abstract: Securing the Internet of Things (IoT) requires detecting and responding to evolving threats across distributed devices with limited computing and communication resources. Large language models (LLMs) can interpret security alerts and help investigate incidents. Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) extends these capabilities by combining reasoning, planning, memory, and tool use to coordinate security actions. Existing studies offer a fragmented account of how these capabilities fit IoT architectures, what risks arise when agents act autonomously, and how to evaluate their performance. This survey addresses these gaps by tracing the transition from LLM-assisted analysis to agentic defence across threat detection, triage, investigation, and response. We develop a unified taxonomy covering IoT infrastructure, LLM-driven and agentic security, trust and resilience, application domains, and evaluation methods. We compare hierarchical, orchestration-based, distributed multi-agent, and cognitive architectures by examining where security decisions are made, how agents coordinate, and where actions are executed across device, edge, fog, and cloud layers. We also examine threats introduced by agentic operation, including prompt injection, memory poisoning, privacy leakage, and compromised trust between agents, together with corresponding defences. Our synthesis finds that limited attack testing and dataset coverage leave uncertainty about how well these systems generalize, while coordination failures and inference overhead constrain deployment. These findings motivate research on trustworthy orchestration, privacy-preserving collaboration, explainable security decisions, and efficient edge inference.

paper_title: Climate Change and Malaria Transmission in Cameroon: Ten-Model CMIP6 Projections, VECTRI Simulations and a Regional Evaluation Against Routine and Survey Data
paper_abstract: For Cameroon, projections of climate change effects on malaria at the administrative scale of the national programme, confronted with surveillance data, are lacking. We combined a rule-based climatic suitability analysis driven by ten bias-adjusted NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 models under SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5 with simulations of the VECTRI malaria model forced by the most representative ensemble member (EC-Earth3), aggregated the results to the 10 regions and 58 departments, and evaluated the uncalibrated model against routine (2019-2024) and survey (2022) data. All models warm Cameroon (median +1.2 °C by mid-century under SSP2-4.5 and +4.0 °C by 2081-2100 under SSP5-8.5). The rule-based suitable season changes little, except under SSP5-8.5 at the end of the century, when months above 34 °C shorten it in the Far North. VECTRI simulates a higher entomological inoculation rate in every scenario (+43% to +188%), significant in all 58 departments and largest in the western highlands and on the Adamawa plateau. The model did not reproduce the regional ranking of routine incidence; it reproduced the north-south gradient of seasonality (Spearman ρ = 0.79, Holm-adjusted p = 0.015), but not the bimodal southern cycle. Calibration, district-level evaluation and an ensemble of forcing models are needed before these projections can inform early warning.

paper_title: Safety Frontiers in Professional Mechanical Plaque Removal (PMPR): A Scoping Review of Current Evidence
paper_abstract: Background: Professional mechanical plaque removal (PMPR) is an established cornerstone of periodontal and peri-implant therapy, yet a comprehensive mapping of its associated iatrogenic risks and hard tissue modifications remains methodologically fragmented. This scoping review mapped the current literature regarding the safety profiles and substrate alterations resulting from contemporary PMPR modalities. Methods: Conducted in strict adherence to Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and PRISMA-ScR guidelines, a literature search was executed on PubMed/MEDLINE without date restrictions. Eligible studies were screened based on predefined Population, Concept, and Context (PCC) criteria. Two independent reviewers performed a two-stage screening process, with consensus achieved via a third reviewer. Results: From 97 initially identified records, full-text evaluation of 18 eligible articles yielded 5 pivotal studies meeting all quantitative safety criteria. The evidence demonstrates that substrate alterations—including surface roughness, abrasive wear, and structural degradation across enamel, dentin, cementum, and titanium—are critically dependent on device selection, application force, tip geometry, and powder abrasivity. Conclusions: Contemporary PMPR modalities demonstrate a high degree of clinical safety when operated within standardized thresholds; however, iatrogenic substrate degradation remains critically dependent on device selection and application parameters. Establishing standardized quantitative safety metrics is imperative to systematically minimize surface trauma while preserving anatomical and biomaterial integrity.

paper_title: Nutritional Strategies for Managing Gastrointestinal Adverse Effects Associated with GLP-1 Receptor Agonist and Dual GIP/GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Therapy: A Narrative Review with Practical Recommendations
paper_abstract: Incretin-based therapies have marked a turning point in the treatment of obesity, because of their demonstrated effects on body weight and beyond, including numerous cardi-ometabolic outcomes. Within obesity management, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) and dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP)/GLP-1 receptor agonists (GIP/GLP-1 RAs) are, to date, the most effective pharma-cological strategies. A growing body of evidence, however, points to limited tolerability caused by gastrointestinal adverse effects, which may impair treatment adherence and reduce both quality of life and the nutritional adequacy of patients’ diets. These effects, which include nausea, vomiting, dyspepsia, constipation, diarrhea, and abdominal bloating, are often observed in the early phases of treatment and during dose escalation. Yet the dietary recommendations available for their management remain fragmentary and inaccurate. This narrative review sets out to analyze the main pathophysiological mechanisms un-derlying the gastrointestinal manifestations of incretin-based therapies and to gather the available evidence on nutritional strategies for their prevention and management. We address the contribution of the GLP-1 and GIP systems to the modulation of gastroin-testinal motility, appetite, and clinical tolerability, with attention to the differences cur-rently recognized between selective GLP-1 RAs and dual GIP/GLP-1 RAs. We then present practical, symptom-specific recommendations covering meal distribution, mod-ulation of fat and fiber intake, hydration, food choices, and the overall quality of diet and lifestyle. Finally, we discuss the key role of nutrition in preservation adequate energy and protein intake, preventing micronutrient deficiencies, and conserving muscle mass throughout treatment with incretin-based therapies. A structured, personalized, symptom-oriented nutritional approach could improve the tolerability of these therapies, optimize clinical outcomes, and support their efficacy over the long term.

paper_title: Pulmonary Nodule Management: A Narrative Review of Clinical Decision-Making and Continuity of Care
paper_abstract: Management of pulmonary nodules detected on computed tomography requires assessment of malignancy risk, treatment suitability and the benefits and harms of available options. This narrative review examines clinical decision-making and continuity of care for screening-detected and incidental nodules. Core searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science and the Cochrane Library covered English-language literature from 2010 through August 2026, supplemented by targeted searches and citation tracing. Evidence was selectively synthesized around management decisions. Nodule type, prior imaging and consistent measurement methods guide risk assessment and surveillance. Surveillance intervals and intervention criteria remain specific to the detection setting, the nodule type and the applicable management framework. Further testing is appropriate when its results could change a feasible management plan; negative or nondiagnostic results require interpretation in light of residual malignancy risk. Treatment selection should balance expected benefit against procedural harm and overtreatment, considering cardiopulmonary reserve, frailty, comorbidity, competing mortality risks and patient preferences. Within the reviewed literature, patient-outcome benefit from artificial intelligence has not been established. Continuity of care requires completion of planned actions, review and communication of results, and clear responsibility for subsequent follow-up. Risk-informed decisions should be linked to reliable follow-up, with reassessment as imaging findings or patient circumstances change.

paper_title: Edge Computing for IoT-Enabled Smart Cities: A Review of Middleware, Explainable AI, and User Behavior Analytics
paper_abstract: This review looks at cloud–IoT edge middleware for analyzing user behavior in smart cities, with a particular focus on linking behavioral analytics to energy-aware and mission-critical urban services. The topic sits at the crossroads of smart-city platforms, IoT sensing, edge/fog/cloud computing, service-oriented architectures, machine learning, explainable AI, privacy-aware governance, and energy-critical applications such as EV charging, energy demand, environmental exposure, crowd safety, and the operational resilience of urban infrastructure. As such, this paper maps out the main categories of user-behavior data, examines five application domains, compares several case studies, and puts forward a new XAI-EdgeSOA Middleware Framework called X-EdgeCity Middleware. This framework brings together IoT sensing, edge preprocessing, fog coordination, event-driven communication, cloud analytics, XAI explanations, privacy-by-design, and benchmark logging. The goal is to support not just general smart-city applications, but also energy-sensitive or mission-critical services, where latency, reliability, explainability, and accountability have a direct impact on urban safety and continuity of operations.

paper_title: PrivacyPR: A Dataset of Real-World Privacy Fixes for Benchmarking Privacy-Aware Code Review
paper_abstract: Coding agents increasingly review code, yet whether they catch the privacy defects that laws such as the GDPR require software to avoid remains largely untested, partly because few datasets connect real privacy defects to their accepted fixes and review context. We present PrivacyPR, a dataset of 4,131 merged GitHub pull requests (PRs) from 1,469 repositories, created between June 2018 and January 2024. Each PR includes its commits, diffs, review discussion, and LLM-generated labels for privacy relevance, fix type, and GDPR principles. PrivacyPR provides 1,169 high-confidence privacy fixes and 1,643 non-fix PRs, together with Verified, a manually checked split of 250 privacy fixes and 250 non-fix PRs, and Small, a 100 + 100 subset for evaluation. On Verified, both annotators endorsed 72% of the LLM's GDPR-principle assignments. Beyond supporting empirical study of how privacy defects arise and are fixed, PrivacyPR provides a benchmark for privacy-aware code review on real, developer-accepted fixes. Its evaluation harness reverts each fix to reintroduce the defect. On Small, two coding agents detect only 42-51% of defects under a generic review prompt, but 88-91% when explicitly asked to check privacy, while flagging 11-15% of non-fix PRs. These results show that privacy defects can be detected by coding agents, but that detection depends strongly on review intent and comes with false alarms. Data, code, reviews, judge verdicts, and an extensible evaluation harness are publicly available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23744765.

paper_title: Multimodal Fusion: A Review of Breast Cancer Advanced and Traditional Modalities
paper_abstract: Purpose: Multimodal medical imaging fusion (MMIF) is an increasingly important approach to breast cancer detection (BCD), as different imaging modalities rely on different physical principles and provide complementary information. No single modality can capture all the structural, functional, and biological information needed for accurate diagnosis and characterization. Methods: This review examines more than 15 imaging modalities used in breast cancer detection, including conventional techniques such as mammography, ultrasound, and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), as well as emerging approaches such as thermal imaging, photoacoustic imaging, microwave imaging, and multimodal microscopy. Results: Mammography, ultrasound, and MRI remain among the most widely used modalities, providing complementary structural and functional information. Recent AI advances have enabled fusion at the data, feature, and decision levels, with applications in detection, classification, segmentation, prognosis, and personalized cancer management. Multimodal approaches increasingly combine imaging data with clinical, histopathological, and genomic information. However, important challenges remain, including limited availability of large and diverse multimodal datasets, variations in imaging protocols, missing modalities, limited external validation, and the need for interpretable and clinically reliable AI models. Conclusion: MMIF offers promising opportunities to improve breast cancer detection and characterization by combining complementary imaging and non-imaging information. Future research should prioritize robust fusion strategies, standardized and diverse datasets, multicenter validation, explainable and privacy-preserving AI, and the integration of imaging with clinical and molecular data to facilitate reliable translation into clinical practice.

paper_title: Explainable AI for MRI Brain Tumor Classification: A Scoping Review of Clinical Validation
paper_abstract: Machine learning and deep learning models for magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based brain tumor classification now report accuracies above 98% on public benchmarks, yet clinical use has not followed. Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) is presented as the bridge, but whether the explanations are correct is seldom tested. This scoping review, following PRISMA-ScR-compatible reporting conventions, searched PubMed, IEEE Xplore, SpringerLink, ScienceDirect and Google Scholar on 13 July 2026 for studies published from 2020 to 2026. Of 105 screened records, 50 primary studies and 12 reviews were included. The 22 primary studies extracted at full text were audited with a five-level explanation-validation hierarchy and a nine-item reporting-integrity instrument, organised around five research questions. Twelve of the 22 studies applied no explanation; seven assessed explanations by visual narration, one against a segmentation mask and two with internal faithfulness metrics. None validated explanations against radiologist annotation (0/22; 95% CI 0–15.4%). Median best accuracies were similar for handcrafted (98.5%), hybrid (98.7%) and end-to-end deep pipelines (98.1%). Only two studies reported a verifiable patient-level split, three validated externally, two released code, two reported calibration, and four reported headline figures inconsistent with their own data. Interpretability is better described by where it sits in the pipeline, and whether it has been checked, than by the modelling paradigm. We summarise tumor types, imaging modalities, classification and segmentation methods and public datasets, and propose a 12-item checklist that makes agreement with expert annotation, patient-level partitioning and deployment cost routine reporting items.

paper_title: A Comprehensive Review of the Physics Involved in Modelling Transport Phenomena Associated with Extrusion-Deposition Additive Manufacturing Process
paper_abstract: The dilemma of most upcoming researchers in the field of fiber reinforced polymer (FRP) composite processing is not the lack or accessibility to relevant background literature but rather their comprehensive nature, or their applicability to the specific needs of the researcher. Most existing literature either target just a specific modeling aspect or present high-level overview of the overall FRP process which lacks necessary underlying physics, coupling across hierarchical physics scales and computational techniques needed to improve on existing process simulation tools without necessarily reinventing the wheel. The current review article presents detailed understanding of the overall FRP composite process, the relevant transport phenomena and underlying physics across various scales and current trends in computational solution techniques used to predict FRP composite melt-flow phenomena in order to develop well equipped process-structure-property (PSP) maps for improved process monitoring and optimized print properties and performance. The overall position of potential research opportunities from survey of existing simulation efforts includes (i) the refinement of existing and development of new quantitative and qualitative multiscale models for predicting transport phenomena, (ii) development of new closed-form tensor evolution equations and constitutive relations with new information of the bulk fiber and melt-flow field states, and (iii) proper model benchmarking with experimental observation from in-situ process monitoring, and development of machine learning tools for the creation of a robust PSP map.

paper_title: Atypical and Exceptional Hematological Presentations of Vitamin B12 (Cobalamin) Deficiency: A Review of Case Reports and a Practical Diagnostic Approach
paper_abstract: Vitamin B12 (cobalamin) deficiency is classically recognized by macrocytic anemia, but a minority of patients present with life-threatening or misleading hematological pictures. In a series of 201 consecutive patients, about 10% had severe manifestations, including symptomatic pancytopenia, pseudo-thrombotic microangiopathy (pseudo-TMA) and hemolytic anemia. Case reports describe further presentations that mimic thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP), myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS), acute leukemia, Evans syndrome and immune thrombocytopenia, or that present with venous thrombosis, including cerebral venous sinus thrombosis. The resulting diagnostic errors expose patients to plasma exchange, corticosteroids, marrow-directed work-up and central venous access. Drawing on a targeted narrative review, we summarise reported phenotypes, identify features that may distinguish these presentations from their mimics, and propose a parallel diagnostic approach incorporating serum B12 and, when indicated, methylmalonic acid (MMA), total homocysteine and holotranscobalamin. Testing must not delay emergency treatment for suspected TTP. The evidence consists of isolated observations and one consecutive single-center series, and should be read as a prompt for vigilance rather than as a measure of frequency.

paper_title: Cross-Infection of Rhizobia in Leguminous Plants: Host Range, Nitrogen Fixation and Agricultural Benefits - A Review
paper_abstract: Inoculating legume plants with indigenous rhizobial strains provides a foundation for evaluating their host compatibility and ability to adapt to different environmental conditions. Evaluating the ability of rhizobial strains to nodulate different legume species helps determine their suitability for application as biological inoculants. Cross-infectious, host range, and nitrogen fixation are the main aspects of plant-microbe symbiosis in legume-rhizobia interactions. Cross-infectivity is described as the ability of a microbial strain that is associated with multiple host plants, while host range refers to the spectrum of compatible plant species. Effectiveness of this process depends on the compatibility between host and strain, effectiveness of the formation of nodule, and physical environmental conditions such as soil nutrient status and climate. Expanding host range through cross-infective strains has significant implications for sustainable agriculture, such as improving crop yields in nitrogen-limited soils and reducing fertilizers. Therefore, this review merges the recent knowledge on the fundamental cross-infectivity and host range, and their direct impact on nitrogen fixation efficiency. It further explores advances in molecular biology and genomics that aim to manipulate these interactions for enhanced agricultural productivity. Understanding how host compatibility influences the effectiveness of rhizobial symbiosis is important for understanding the interaction between host specificity and symbiotic performance which is essential for development of effective bio-inoculants and promoting ecological sustainability in the agricultural system.

paper_title: Delays in Early Defibrillation in Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: A Scoping Review from a Systems and Public Health Perspective
paper_abstract: Background/Objectives: Early defibrillation is critical for survival after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA), yet delays arise from interacting community, organizational, dispatch, and emergency medical services (EMS) factors. This scoping review mapped determinants of delayed defibrillation, examined temporal measurement approaches, and summarized associations with clinical outcomes. Methods: A preregistered scoping review was conducted following Joanna Briggs Institute guidance and PRISMA-ScR reporting standards. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and CINAHL were searched in February 2026. Two reviewers independently screened records, and extracted data were cross-checked. Evidence was synthesized descriptively across system-level domains and temporal categories. Results: Of 4456 records identified, 82 studies were included, predominantly observational (75/82, 91.5%). Determinants were classified as community-related (32/82, 39.0%), system-related (26/82, 31.7%), dispatch-related (18/82, 22.0%), and EMS-related (6/82, 7.3%). Fifty-two studies reported classifiable temporal metrics. Among 48 studies linking timing or early-defibrillation determinants with outcomes, 31 examined direct or multiple shock-related intervals, two examined upstream operational response times, and 15 used indirect indicators. Of the 31 studies assessing direct or multiple shock-related intervals, 30 (96.8%) indicated more favorable outcomes with shorter timing. All 28 studies using a single direct shock-related interval showed directional concordance. Conclusion. Defibrillation delays reflect interconnected system-level processes rather than EMS response time alone. Standardized temporal measurement, integrated AED and responder networks, and targeted strategies addressing geographic and socioeconomic disparities may support earlier defibrillation. These findings have implications for emergency-care organization, interprofessional coordination, and nursing education in resuscitation systems.

paper_title: ArchSpace: Recording, Reviewing, and Referencing LLM Architecture Research
paper_abstract: Model architecture shapes the scaling behavior, training efficiency, and inference cost of LLMs, making it a central focus of both industry and academia. In industry, teams such as those behind DeepSeek, Qwen, and Kimi routinely introduce architectural innovations, yet public reports rarely document which ideas succeeded, which were abandoned, and why. In academia, limited compute and inconsistent baselines often restrict evaluations to small-scale, single-point comparisons, making it difficult to establish whether improvements hold at larger scales or translate into broader impact. ArchSpace addresses both gaps as a public platform for Recording, Reviewing, and Referencing Architecture Research: each proposal is recorded with its experiments and reasoning, reviewed by the community, and referenced by later work. To evaluate ideas before costly large-scale training, ArchSpace leverages scaling laws to predict model loss at larger scales from smaller experiments, a practice widely adopted in industry. We provide initial references that make the platform usable: Qwen3.5 and OLMo3 baselines, fitted scaling laws, and a reusable training recipe. Ideas validated through this review can in turn become new baselines, and ArchSpace thereby aims to broaden the range of ideas that shape the next generation of models.

paper_title: Geometric Properties of Human High-Performing Buildings: A Review of the Evidence and the Implications for Practice
paper_abstract: Building performance is conventionally assessed in structural, thermal, energy, and functional terms, while architectural character is treated as a matter of taste. Yet a growing body of research suggests that the geometric characteristics of buildings also affect performance experienced directly by people—perceptual engagement, restoration and well-being, perceived safety, social affordance, and patterns of movement and use—both within buildings and in adjoining streets and public spaces. This paper reviews that evidence and develops a conceptual model and theoretical account of how the relevant characteristics arise. Drawing on environmental psychology, experimental aesthetics, neuroaesthetics, urban design, and the mathematics of form, it identifies recurring geometric characteristics associated with favorable human responses, centered on symmetry and symmetry-breaking, multiscale organization, and contextual relationship. It proposes that these are traces of generative processes rather than attributes of style, and it introduces “deep symmetry”: a progression of correspondence from the isolated object through scale and context to the perceiving human participant, with a candidate mechanism grounded in embodied perception and processing fluency. The framework reframes stylistic debates as questions of human performance, geometry, and process, and sets out a falsifiable research agenda, candidate measures, and broader implications for practice.

paper_title: Nodding Syndrome: Nursing Leadership and Health Policy Amid Aetiological Uncertainty—A Structured Narrative Review
paper_abstract: Background/Objectives: Nodding syndrome is a disabling neurological condition affecting communities in East Africa. Although its aetiology remains uncertain, affected individuals and families have substantial care needs. This review examined evidence relevant to nursing leadership, service coordination and health policy. Methods: We conducted a structured narrative synthesis of 31 reports directly addressing nodding syndrome and six contextual reports, identified through four bibliographic databases and supplementary sources up to 30 September 2026. Design-specific Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal informed interpretation using Walt and Gilson’s health policy triangle. This was not a formal systematic review. Results: The literature documents needs in seizure management, continuity of antiseizure medicines, rehabilitation, follow-up, caregiver support, stigma reduction and community trust. Barriers include medicine shortages, transport costs, fragmented referrals and resource constraints. Nursing activities recur across education, surveillance, follow-up and coordination, but studies rarely isolate the effects of nurse-led care. Evidence for nodding-syndrome-specific prevention remains insufficient. Conclusions: Aetiological uncertainty does not remove the responsibility to organize essential care. Nursing coordination and community participation are evidence-informed proposals for addressing documented service gaps, but their clinical effectiveness, feasibility, equity and sustainability require prospective evaluation. Proposed service models should not be presented as proven interventions or as preventing nodding syndrome.

paper_title: Review of Innovative MOSFET Architectures for Low Power and High Performance Applications
paper_abstract: Semiconductor devices are pivotal technologies for almost all existing industrial sectors, as demonstrated by the recent chips shortages. The limits in scaling, performance and power consumption of electronic components, combined with the strong growth of ICT share in global electrical energy consumption, have put forward the need for alternative solutions. In this respect, innovative and disruptive device architectures have played a decisive role over the past 15 years and will continue to do so for future electronic circuits and systems. In this regard, FDSOI, multi-gate devices, nanowires, 2D devices, and 3D device architectures have shown promising electrical properties for many applications. This paper will review and compare innovative MOSFET architectures which are and will be needed for advanced electronic systems, like FDSOI, FinFET, Gate-All-Around, Nanosheets, Forksheet, CFET, and will address potential novel MOS Transistors with other disruptive architectures recently proposed for future high performance and/or low power ICs, such as the GAIA (Gate-All-Inside-and-Around) MOSFET.

paper_title: Universal Versus Risk-Based Screening for Paediatric Keratoconus: Is Current Evidence Sufficient to Guide Clinical Practice? A Critical Narrative Review
paper_abstract: Keratoconus is increasingly recognised in children and adolescents, and early corneal cross-linking can halt its progression, but it remains unclear whether all children or only those with risk factors should be screened. Selected school-based, clinic-based and other population studies have reported prevalence estimates of approximately 0.4–2.7%, although differences in sampling, age distributions and diagnostic definitions limit direct comparisons. First-degree relatives show a high yield of keratoconus on corneal tomographic assessment, and Down syndrome is associated with increased prevalence, although the main registry estimate is not specific to children. Refractive astigmatism and its progression provide practical referral indicators, whereas atopy and eye rubbing do not currently define sufficiently narrow high-yield groups. The proportion of paediatric cases without recognised risk factors remains unknown. Test accuracy in unselected children, the natural history of screen-detected suspect disease and the comparative cost-effectiveness of screening strategies are also uncertain. Current evidence supports active case-finding in defined high-risk groups and corneal tomographic assessment in children with refractive warning signs. Universal screening should be evaluated in selected high-prevalence settings.

paper_title: Decoding Cryptocurrency Cycles: A Systematic Literature Review of Spectral Analysis, Econophysical Signal Processing, and Complexity Frameworks
paper_abstract: The cryptocurrency market constitutes a complex, non-linear financial ecosystem where traditional econometric frameworks frequently struggle to capture abrupt regime shifts and heavy-tailed crash dynamics. To address this gap, this study synthesizes the application of econophysical signal processing and complexity science in decoding digital asset cycles. Guided by the PRISMA 2020 protocol and a five-domain Risk of Bias (RoB) quality appraisal, this Systematic Literature Review evaluates 30 core empirical and methodological studies (within a 51-source bibliography), establishing a taxonomic classification of time-frequency analysis, adaptive signal decomposition, fractal dynamics, and hybrid machine learning architectures with explicit mathematical formulations and performance benchmarks. The findings indicate that wavelet transforms and Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) isolate non-stationary, multi-scale cyclical behaviors more effectively compared to classical Fourier methods. Furthermore, the temporal evolution of informational complexity metrics—such as Lempel-Ziv Complexity, Bandt-Pompe Permutation Entropy, and Approximate Entropy—reveals pre-crash compression of pattern diversity as a consistent empirical precursor to liquidity evaporation. Additionally, integrating adaptive signal decomposition with hybrid deep learning and α-stable Lévy distributions generally improves forecasting accuracy over standalone linear benchmarks, though regularized parsimonious models (e.g., LASSO and ARIMAX) remain competitive under high noise. Ultimately, non-linear signal engineering provides actionable early warning systems for quantitative asset pricing, latency-aware algorithmic trading, and macroprudential regulatory oversight.

paper_title: Can Afforestation, Reforestation and Revegetation Carbon Projects Work in Mountain Landscapes? A Systematic Review of Eligibility, Monitoring, Permanence and Governance Constraints
paper_abstract: Mountains hold large but poorly recognized carbon stocks, yet the carbon-market rules that finance afforestation, reforestation and revegetation (ARR) were developed for lowland landscapes. Following PRISMA 2020, this systematic review examined whether eligibility, monitoring, permanence and governance requirements work in mountain terrain. Four bibliographic databases, institutional repositories and carbon-standard registries were searched for 2000–2026. Of 5040 records, 185 sources were included, covering five mountain regions, with the Indian Himalayan Region as the principal case.
